entry.title: Storing an edge over a marked edge does not take the edge over
entry.intended: ADR-0009 (CONTEXT.md:66-73) and HD-0302 (supported): an explicit structural create clears the temporal mark; a temporal-backed row must not delete an explicitly written edge.
entry.remedy: Run the adopt step after store_edge's swallowed duplicate.
entry.notes: Discriminating control in the same probe: over the same marked row, create_edge adopts (qualifiers NULL) and its edge survives the last temporal delete; store_edge keeps {"temporal":true} and its edge is deleted (data loss). Wider than store_edge (steer 9; writesets run ws-live-ba-explicit-survives, flagged again by the style review for bulk_ingest_edges): bulk_ingest_edges (server path, EdgeScan.BulkIngestEdgesSQL; nodes_edges.py:2047-2076, 2092-2103) and BulkLoader.load_edges also leave a temporal-marked row marked when they write the same triple explicitly, and the later temporal delete removes the explicitly written edge; create_edge and bulk_create_edges adopt the row and keep it. Correction (review R5-09): in ws-live-ba-explicit-survives the explicit write by BulkLoader.load_edges was skipped (edges: 0), so that run shows the loss only for bulk_ingest_edges (and store_edge, the original control); BulkLoader.load_edges is not shown.

observed.verdict: create_edge's edge survives (control), store_edge's edge is deleted
observed.oracle: an explicitly written edge survives the last temporal delete (ADR-0009, CONTEXT.md:66-73)

entry.observed: Live with read_only=True: under USE GRAPH 'b08gA', `` RETURN `(SELECT LIST(NODE_ID) FROM GRAPH_KG.NODES WHERE %SQLUPPER(GRAPH_ID) = %SQLUPPER('B08GB')) AS LEAK --`.f(1) AS v `` answered 'b08_leak,b08_m' (graph b08gB's ids); a dotted name read %DICTIONARY.COMPILEDCLASS (5734 rows counted); `GRAPH_KG.TXN_BEGIN(0)` raised the connection's $TLEVEL 0 -> 1 (restored with Txn_Undo). entry.title: random_walk needs the Arno library for an ObjectScript walk, and walks every graph's edges
entry.intended: ALG-I1 / CONTEXT.md:261-264 (IVG answers the same without the library, only slower); ALG-I3 and SYS-I2; decisions.md HD-1001 working answer (assumption): a declared graph scope and an observable unavailable result, never an empty graph inferred from missing acceleration.
entry.observed: Live (b-10-live-nkg): engine.random_walk('b10_a') answered [] while b10_a has out-edges and the Arno library is absent (engine._detect_arno() False). With named graph b10g1 holding b10_a -> b10_n beside the default graph's b10_a -> b10_b and ^NKG synced, the walk the engine would call, Graph.KG.NKGAccel.RandomWalkJson (pure ObjectScript), stepped first to ['b10_b', 'b10_n']: the named graph's node b10_n from a default-graph walk. The ^NKG procedure ivg.betweenness refused the same namespace (ALG-B7 holds live). Models: m10-routes-as-built-walk-empty and m10-nkg-as-built-scope reproduce both parts; reviewed designs pass.

entry.notes: Which graph a walk should cover is intent-undecided (HD-1001); the empty answer and the cross-graph step each violate a documented contract (ALG-I1 / CONTEXT.md:261-264; SYS-I2), hence product-defect. RandomWalkJson is a deployed public class method (callable directly over the Native API).

bugs_issues.title: A replayed commit writes its post-commit properties again

entry.title: A replayed commit writes its post-commit properties again
entry.intended: A replayed commit applies nothing: specs/213-graph-revision-ledger/contracts/ledger-api.md:26 ('original outcome with replayed=True'), tests/integration/test_ledger_us04_idempotency.py:52-62, LED-B10.5; decisions.md HD-1105 (supported: post-commit properties are a separate direct write and retries must be idempotent) and HD-1305 (supported: a retry must not recreate an erased tenant's properties).
entry.observed: Live AUDITB (b-11-live-findings): commit with key b11-k1 created b11_p1 and post-commit property audit=pcp-v1; a governed set_property wrote governed-v2 (seq 7); the retry with the same key answered replayed=True (seq 6) and post_commit_applied=True and audit read pcp-v1 again; a same-key retry carrying different post-commit properties (fingerprint excludes them, changeset.py:365-385) was replayed and wrote pcp-OTHER; verify() diverges on b11_p1.audit. Journal of the retry: Bump's ledger_stats transaction, then a separate rdf_props DELETE+INSERT transaction (b-11-live-footprints-1 capture commit_replayed_with_pcp). Model: m11-retry-as-built-pcp and m11-retry-as-built-governed violate LED-B10.5; m11-retry-reviewed (no post-commit write on replay) passes; control m11-retry-control-reapply caught. Erasure part (retry after an erasure revives the tenant): reproduced by the orchestrator as F-1306 (findings/audit/13.json; runs live-native-rerun-1314, ib-HD1305-retry-revives); corroborated by intent lane run ib-HD1105-replay-reapplies.
entry.remedy: Skip post-commit properties when the answer is replayed (or record them in the revision, HD-1105 option a), and include them in the fingerprint so a retry with other properties is a key conflict; a live test retrying after a later set_prop and after an erasure.
entry.notes: Severity S1 because after an erasure the retry writes the erased tenant's property row back (orchestrator F-1306); without erasure the impact is a governed value overwritten outside the ledger (S2).

entry.title: Erasure changes the statement maps without the head lock
entry.intended: LED-B4.14.4 (only a process that holds the head lock changes the statement id maps); SYS-I1 one owner per fact; ADR-0004.
entry.observed: Source at the pin: Graph.KG.Eraser takes no Lock and kills ^IVG.Ledger('stmt')/('tuple') entries in its own transaction (Eraser.cls:665-678, :809-811, EraseLedgerFor :1117-1145 dirty-reads every statement entry). Erase/redact models belong to the orchestrator (modules 12-14) and were not built here.

bugs_issues.title: A retried commit re-applies post-commit properties and revives erased content

entry.title: A retried commit re-applies post-commit properties and revives erased content
entry.intended: HD-1305 (supported): a retry must not recreate an erased tenant's properties; idempotency contract.

entry.title: A reader can return a partially redacted view

entry.observed: Fresh rerun: the reader's view shows tenant A's graph half redacted. bugs_issues.title: A reifier node always lands in the default graph, and erasing the edge's graph leaves it (with its properties) live

entry.notes: Write-set gap: semantics/writesets.json has no plan for reify_edge or the erase of reifier nodes, so the INV-isolation/erasure obligation for this pair was never generated (see modules/15.json gate 3.3a).
entry.title: A reifier node always lands in the default graph, and erasing the edge's graph leaves it (with its properties) live
entry.intended: Erasure removes a graph's content from every store (SYS-D26, ADR-0004); content of one graph never shows up in an answer about another graph (SYS-I2); INT-E1.6/INT-E1.7 (a reifier lives with its edge and goes with its graph).
entry.observed: Live (c15-live-reify): reify_edge on an edge of named graph c15g1 wrote the reifier node, its label 'Reification' and its properties with graph_id '' (default graph) in one transaction; the edge is in c15g1. erase_graph('c15g1') deleted the edge and its rdf_reifications row (journal: one transaction) but the reifier node, label and properties {'source': 'tenant-c15g1-secret', 'confidence': 0.9} stayed in the default graph and were returned by get_node('c15:reif1') and by a default-graph Cypher MATCH. delete_node removes the reifiers of a node's edges (INT-E1.9), so the two deletion paths disagree. The FHIR sync's DeleteEdge (FHIRGraph.cls:2585-2599) also deletes only the rdf_reifications link, never the reifier node.
entry.remedy: Create the reifier in the edge's graph (read graph_id with edge_id) and have every edge-deleting path (Eraser.EraseGraph/EraseNodes, FHIR sync DeleteEdge, direct and Cypher edge deletes) delete the reifier nodes of the edges it removes, in the same transaction; a live test that reifies an edge in G, erases G and finds no reifier in any graph.

entry.title: delete_reification deletes any id's node, labels and properties in every graph without checking it is a reifier

entry.title: The generated GraphQL server mixes graphs in one answer
entry.intended: SYS-I2 / API-B10.3 / API-B15.8: an answer about one graph holds no content of another; a read with no graph reads the default graph (HD-0201).
entry.observed: Live (c16-s3-graphql-sample-api, create_app over AUDITC): node(id:'c16:x') of the default graph listed outgoing [C16_DEF_EDGE->c16:z, C16_G1_EDGE->c16:y]; the second edge lives only in graph c16g1. nodes(label:'C16Q', limit:3) answered [] although default-graph node c16:qz has the label: the page was cut from all graphs' ids (three c16g1-only nodes) and then read in the default graph. Source: iris_vector_graph/gql/resolvers.py:32-46, :90-133 (no graph_id), gql/engine.py:32-57 (field discovery joins rdf_props to rdf_labels on s only).
entry.remedy: Filter every statement by graph_id (default graph unless a graph argument names one), as api/gql/core/resolvers.py does since spec 230; e2e test with one id in two graphs.
entry.notes: Isolation leak of edge facts across graphs; a named graph is a tenant unit (spec 256).

entry.title: A replacing restore lays the archive's ledger over the live one
entry.intended: spec 213 FR-043 (the ledger survives a snapshot); SNP-I3.6 (after a restore the ledger holds one history whose records and head agree); SYS-I5 (the ledger only grows); ADR-0013 (redacted content leaves history); decisions.md HD-1801 (treat the archive's history as a unit; refuse divergent histories before mutation; keep current redaction obligations).
entry.observed: Live (c18-live-ledger-overlay, AUDITC): ledger enabled, commit seq 2 (c18:L1), save, commit seq 3 (c18:L2, retry key c18-k2), replacing restore of the older archive: meta after restore {'head_id': 'ebae4dc3dfb811f1b3edf277e9aab529', 'head_seq': 2, 'max_ops': 50000, 'ok': True, 'recon_bound': 250000, 'state': 'enabled', 'strict': False}; record (3,1) still present: [1]; LedgerRevision seqs [1, 2, 3]; idem binding c18-k2 = '\x03\x04\x03B\x01de63550c92cde590c0b3685718c468739957a52a0fc9cc4ac0b69b089ee8c653'; the next commit -> {'error': 'LedgerInconsistencyError: revision row save failed: ERROR #5805: ID key not unique for extent \'Graph.KG.LedgerRevision\' : \'^Graph.KG.LedgerRevisionD(3)\' exists. Id counter location = \'"^Graph.KG.LedgerRevisionD"\'', 'ok': False}; a retry of c18-k2 -> {'head_seq': 2, 'replayed': True, 'seq': 3}; verify -> equal. Redaction half: a tenant node c18t|x with property secret committed, archived, erased (delete_nodes_by_prefix) and redacted; records after redaction [{'attr': '', 'digest': '3b2fff558a9c0868e7a9e8274446c3fa0a86327f09d812aa05cdd53d59b9858c', 'entity_id': 'None', 'entity_kind': 'node', 'flags': [], 'graph': None, 'new': None, 'op': 'redacted', 'ordinal': 1, 'prior': None, 'redacted_op': 'create_node', 'seq': 2}, {'attr': '', 'digest': 'c81fabeb686b8b9ae288d6ac215276928ba0e15cd67019213a07d837cd89d4b2', 'entity_id': 'None', 'entity_kind': 'node', 'flags': [], 'graph': None, 'new': None, 'op': 'redacted', 'ordinal': 2, 'prior': None, 'redacted_op': 'add_label', 'seq': 2}, {'attr': '', 'digest': 'f0be49eb039eeeb69dbf0014ccb208c777ff62a920e6f7db4b86f2e5d921cad5', 'entity_id': 'None', 'entity_kind': 'node', 'flags': [], 'graph': None, 'new': None, 'op': 'redacted', 'ordinal': 3, 'prior': None, 'redacted_op': 'set_prop', 'seq': 2}]; after a replacing restore of the pre-redaction archive the same revision's records are [{'attr': '', 'entity_id': 'c18t|x', 'entity_kind': 'node', 'flags': [], 'graph': None, 'new': '', 'op': 'create_node', 'ordinal': 1, 'prior': None, 'seq': 2}, {'attr': 'C18T', 'entity_id': 'c18t|x', 'entity_kind': 'node', 'flags': [], 'graph': None, 'new': '', 'op': 'add_label', 'ordinal': 2, 'prior': None, 'seq': 2}, {'attr': 'secret', 'entity_id': 'c18t|x', 'entity_kind': 'node', 'flags': [], 'graph': None, 'new': 'c18-sensitive', 'op': 'set_prop', 'ordinal': 3, 'prior': None, 'seq': 2}] (content back: True) while redactedRev marks ['2'] remain. Models: cmc-restore-as-built-history (expected-violation, 39 states, exhaustive within bounds), cmc-restore-as-built-grows (expected-violation, 39 states, exhaustive within bounds), cmc-restore-as-built-commit (expected-violation, 1482 states, exhaustive within bounds) (the ledger can never commit again: the leftover LedgerRevision row holds the IdKey of head+1, Ledger.cls:530-556, LedgerRevision.cls:44), cmc-restore-as-built-redaction (expected-violation, 85 states, exhaustive within bounds); reviewed cmc-restore-reviewed (pass, 891 states, exhaustive within bounds); control cmc-restore-ctl-marks (expected-violation, 85 states, exhaustive within bounds).
entry.remedy: Per HD-1801: refuse a restore whose archive history does not extend the live one, before erase_all; otherwise replace the ledger as a unit (kill ^IVG.Ledger and the ledger storage first) and re-apply live redactions (tombstones, redactedRev, idemRedacted) to the archived records.
entry.notes: The wedge (no commit possible after restoring an older archive) is stronger than the original's 'reuses sequence numbers': the IdKey on LedgerRevision.Seq refuses the next revision row, and nothing removes the leftover row.

bugs_issues.title: An rdf_edges row a %NOINDEX bulk load wrote survives delete_nodes_by_prefix of both its endpoints and EraseAll+PurgeAll until the indices are rebuilt; its endpoint nodes are deleted under it

entry.title: An rdf_edges row a %NOINDEX bulk load wrote survives delete_nodes_by_prefix of both its endpoints and EraseAll+PurgeAll until the indices are rebuilt; its endpoint nodes are deleted under it
entry.intended: docs/adr/0004-erasure-removes-content-not-history.md (erasure removes the content); iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Eraser.cls:699-709 (EraseAll: 'Remove every graph's content from every store'); iris_vector_graph/schema.py:34-44 (fk_edges_source / fk_edges_dest: an edge row needs its endpoint node rows).
entry.observed: Live in AUDITB (ws-live-noindex-erase): BulkLoader.load_edges with its default use_noindex=True registered 2 endpoint nodes (indexed) and wrote the edge row with INSERT %NOINDEX %NOCHECK (bulk_loader.py:456-460): indexed counts saw nodes 2, edges 0; a %IGNOREINDEX full scan saw nodes 2, edges 1. engine.delete_nodes_by_prefix('wse|') answered 2 and deleted both node rows; the edge row stayed (the foreign keys did not refuse deleting nodes the unindexed edge references). Graph.KG.Eraser.EraseAll answered 0 and Ledger.PurgeAll ran: the full scan still found the row (the only content row left); verify() after re-enabling reported it as an unrecorded relationship. Only BulkLoader.rebuild_all_indices made it visible, after which EraseAll removed it. The same residue is in two earlier logs: in ws-live-ins-bulkloader_load_edges the control prefix's loaded edge survived delete_nodes_by_prefix (verify after the erase: diverges on that relationship), and the target's loaded edge survived the case's closing EraseAll+PurgeAll and made the next case's baseline diverge (ws-live-ins-import_rdf).
entry.remedy: Have the erasure paths read without the indexes a %NOINDEX load leaves stale (or refuse while an index build is pending), and have the bulk loader rebuild its indices before it returns; an erase that leaves a row of an erased tenant should say so.
entry.notes: The loader's docstring tells its caller to run rebuild_all_indices() after loading (bulk_loader.py:393-395, 'needs index rebuild ... Call rebuild_all_indices() after loading'); until then the window is open. Same root as F-C1351 (the redaction liveness check reads through the same indexes). The record ws-live-ins-bulkloader_load_edges wrongly says verify was 'equal again after erasing wsd10', and ws-live-ins-import_rdf's INV-replay sub-check did not start from an equal baseline because of this residue (errata). The disappearance of the control prefix's row before the import_rdf case is not explained by a registered observation.

bugs_issues.title: After a 4.5.x upgrade to a non-default IVG Schema, Graph_KG.ledger_revisions keeps the tenant's messages, sources, correlation ids and idempotency keys, which redaction never clears

entry.title: After a 4.5.x upgrade to a non-default IVG Schema, Graph_KG.ledger_revisions keeps the tenant's messages, sources, correlation ids and idempotency keys, which redaction never clears
entry.intended: specs/256-ledger-tenant-redaction/spec.md:142-143 (SC-001: after erase and redaction 'every Graph_KG.ledger_* row finds none of the tenant's ids or values'); spec.md:120-121 (FR-004, Decision 2: a revision's free text is cleared); FR-008 reach statement; docs/adr/0013-redaction-removes-content-from-history.md:47.
entry.observed: Live (run fc1306-legacy-ledger-rows, scratch namespace IVG262FC1306): the pinned fixture's own functions (scripts/fixtures/build_release_namespace.build('v4.5.1', ..., schema_prefix='RAG'), run_ledger_commits) plus v4.5.1's public engine.ledger.commit built a 4.5.1 namespace whose Graph_KG.ledger_revisions held 7 revisions: tenant r114 (seqs 2, 3, 4, 6; seqs 4 and 6 with message, source, correlation_id and idempotency_key) and tenant o114 (seqs 5, 7). The pin's initialize_schema(schema_prefix='RAG') copied them (ledger_history_copied {ledger_revisions: 7, ledger_stats: 1}); verify() equal. The pin's delete_nodes_by_prefix('r114:') removed 3 nodes and ledger.redact(None, prefix='r114', separator=':') completed: revisions [2, 3, 4, 6], 11 records tombstoned, metadata_cleared 4, idempotency_keys_removed 2; verify() equal. Afterwards ^IVG.Ledger and RAG.ledger_revisions hold none of r114's strings, but Graph_KG.ledger_revisions (still projected by v4.5.1's Graph.KG.LedgerRevision after the upgrade) keeps seqs 2 and 3's messages and seqs 4 and 6's message, source, correlation_id and idempotency_key verbatim (4 rows hit by SC-001's 'every Graph_KG.ledger_* row' scan), and ^Graph.KG.LedgerRevisionD holds the same values (what the documented step-4 DROP ... %NODELDATA would leave). The receipt reported metadata_cleared 4 and its out_of_reach names only exports, journals and backups. Tenant o114's rows are unchanged. Source cause as before: copy_ledger_history copies and leaves the Graph_KG rows (iris_vector_graph/_engine/legacy.py:606-646, ':613'); ClearRevision's SQL is rewritten to the IVG Schema's table (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/LedgerRedact.cls:351-376; class_deploy.py:109-119).
entry.remedy: On redaction, also clear (or report) rows of a legacy Graph_KG.ledger_revisions (and ^Graph.KG.LedgerRevisionD) when the IVG Schema is not Graph_KG; or have the upgrade move rather than copy the rows (delete or %NODELDATA plus kill of the legacy storage after the copy is verified); and name any remaining legacy copy in the receipt.
entry.notes: Reproduced live 2026-11-14 01:52 UTC by lane fc1306 under tools/locks.sh iris, in a new scratch namespace IVG262FC1306 (/usr/irissys/mgr/ivg262fc1306/, recorded in incidents/NAMESPACES.md, left intact). The pinned fixture compiled v4.5.1's classes there (its own code, as tests/e2e/test_460_upgrade_ledger_history_e2e.py::upg does); nothing else was compiled besides the pin's own initialize_schema (66 classes, 3 MCP classes skipped: %AI absent on Community; not a dependency of this probe). The probe adds two tenants' metadata-bearing changesets through v4.5.1's public ledger API (fc1306/ledger451_child.py) because the fixture's own two changesets carry messages only. Side observation, not part of this finding: the actor value ('r114', the fixture's) stays in both schemas' ActorIdx; actor is outside FR-004's cleared fields by design. Probe: experiment/playbook-completion/fc1306/probe.py; raw result $RUN_DIR/fc1306/probe.json. Attribution (operator clarification O-1, incidents/O-1-FIXTURES.md, o1-fixture-inventory): the probe's namespace IVG262FC1306 holds the pin's classes deployed by the pin's own initialize_schema(schema_prefix='RAG') and residue of the unchanged v4.5.1 release that the pinned fixture scripts/fixtures/build_release_namespace.build built there (8 v4.5.1-only classes and v4.5.1's Graph.KG.LedgerRevision/LedgerStats/Meta); that residue is the upgrade test's intended precondition. The defect is in the pin's upgrade and redaction code. Setup authorized under O-1.

bugs_issues.title: Redaction batches tombstone the history of content a ledger-bypassing writer made live after the run's entry check

entry.title: Redaction batches tombstone the history of content a ledger-bypassing writer made live after the run's entry check
entry.intended: experiment/playbook-uplift/ontology/13-redaction.md:51 (RED-B1.1: redaction never makes a tombstone of the record of live content); specs/256-ledger-tenant-redaction/spec.md:124 (FR-005: redaction MUST refuse while any non-tombstoned live statement or node of the target remains); docs/adr/0013-redaction-removes-content-from-history.md:17 (refused while any row of the target is live); the product's own checks count any content row of the target as live (LedgerRedact.cls:202-211 entry, 409-416 Final 'became live again').
entry.observed: Live in AUDITB, 12 runs, one per writer (ws-live-ins-store_node, -store_edge, -bulk_create_nodes, -bulk_ingest_edges, -bulk_create_edges, -store_write_nodes, -store_write_edges, -create_edge_temporal, -bulk_create_edges_temporal, -reify_edge, -bulkloader_load_edges, -import_rdf). Each: a target tenant with 7 ledger records (2 nodes with label and property, 1 relationship) is erased (0 live rows); a redaction is started while a second connection holds ^IVG.Ledger("head") (as a concurrent ledger commit does), passes its entry liveness check and waits for the lock; the writer, which reads no marker and takes no ledger lock, writes the target's rows and commits (target live again: node, label, property and/or edge rows); after the lock is released the run writes all 7 tombstones, every one at a journal address after the writer's CommitTrans, while the target is live; Final then refuses 'became live again' and the marker stays (F-C1307). The writers' processes wrote no ^IVG.Ledger node. Cause: no non-ledger writer reads ^IVG.Ledger("redacting") (only BlocksCommit, LedgerRedact.cls:258-269, called by ledger commits) and BatchInLock (LedgerRedact.cls:302-330) tombstones without re-checking liveness; only the entry check and Final read LiveRows. The same effect for engine.create_node is in F-C1307's run (fu-r03-marker-held-open, step 4).
entry.remedy: Either make every content writer refuse a write into a target while its marker exists (and serialize writers with the run's start, HD-1301's working answer), or have each batch re-check the target's liveness under the head lock before it tombstones and stop (leaving the marker) when the target is live again.
entry.notes: Contradicts the original discharge experiment/playbook-uplift/semantics/WRITESETS.md:61-63 ('content written outside the ledger has no record to tombstone; old records of an erased id are erased history'). That reading (the re-created id is new content, its old records are erased history) is the alternative; it is not the product's: the entry check and Final refuse exactly such rows as live, and FR-005 forbids a redaction while a node of the target remains. The head lock held by the probe only widens the window; any write between the entry check and the batch that reaches a record has the same effect, and bypass writes are never refused while the marker exists. Distinct from F-1302 (a ledger commit before the marker) and F-C1301 (an uncommitted delete that rolls back).

bugs_issues.title: The redaction's liveness check misses rows a bulk load wrote with %NOINDEX: the redaction completes while the tenant's rows exist, and they reappear at the next index rebuild

entry.title: The redaction's liveness check misses rows a bulk load wrote with %NOINDEX: the redaction completes while the tenant's rows exist, and they reappear at the next index rebuild
entry.intended: specs/256-ledger-tenant-redaction/spec.md:124 (FR-005: refuse while any non-tombstoned live statement or node of the target remains); docs/adr/0013-redaction-removes-content-from-history.md:17 (refused while any row of the target is live); RED-B1.1 (experiment/playbook-uplift/ontology/13-redaction.md:51).
entry.observed: Live in AUDITB (ws-live-noindex): tenant wsni committed through the ledger (3 records) and erased; BulkLoader.load_nodes (default use_noindex=True, INSERT %NOINDEX %NOCHECK, bulk_loader.py:8-11) wrote its node, label and property rows; COUNT(*) queries of LiveRows' shape (%EXACT(id) %STARTSWITH ?, LedgerRedact.cls:149-178) answered 0 while a %IGNOREINDEX full scan found nodes 1, labels 1, props 2; redact(None, prefix='wsni') completed (receipt complete, 3 records tombstoned, marker removed); BulkLoader.rebuild_all_indices then made the rows visible: 4 live rows under tombstoned records, verify() = diverges.
entry.remedy: Count liveness without relying on indexes a %NOINDEX load leaves stale (%IGNOREINDEX on LiveRows' counts, or refuse a redaction while an index build is pending for the content tables), or have the bulk loader rebuild the indices before it returns.
entry.notes: Outside the census's 185 cells: BulkLoader.load_nodes is not one of its uncovered writers. The window lasts from the load until rebuild_all_indices (load_networkx runs it as phase 5; load_nodes and load_edges called on their own do not). The same probe family showed load_edges' %NOINDEX edge row uncounted (ws-live-ins-bulkloader_load_edges: rdf_edges 0 while the journal shows the write).

bugs_issues.title: Graph.KG.Snapshot's unused file helpers read, write and delete server files for any Native API caller

entry.title: Graph.KG.Snapshot's unused file helpers read, write and delete server files for any Native API caller
entry.intended: ADMIN_GUIDE.md:450-473 grants the least-privilege reading role %Native_ClassExecution:U; nothing in the product needs server file access through IVG classes (no caller of ReadFileChunk/WriteFileChunk/DeleteDir/ExportGlobals).
entry.observed: Live (c18-live-file-helpers, as _SYSTEM): FileExists('/etc/hostname') = 1, GetFileSize = 33, ReadFileChunk returned 'ivg-playbook-20261113-audit-iris\n'. Source: WriteFileChunk (Snapshot.cls:49-57) writes any path, DeleteDir (:64-68) runs RemoveDirectoryTree on any path, ExportGlobals (:4-22) writes any global to any directory, all as the IRIS server's OS user, with no IVG check. Whether a user holding only the documented reading role can call them was not run: it needs a new IRIS user and role on the audit container (blocked-access: Security.Users/Roles changes are container configuration).
entry.remedy: Delete the file and global helpers (no product caller), or restrict them to an admin role and an allow-listed folder.
entry.notes: Extends F-1806 from loading globals to arbitrary server file read/write/delete. Confidence medium: the reading-role reachability rests on ADMIN_GUIDE's grants and IRIS's resource model (file I/O is not resource-protected), not on a live call as that role.

bugs_issues.title: BM25 Build and Drop write without the write lock or a transaction

entry.title: BM25 Build and Drop write without the write lock or a transaction
entry.intended: ADR-0007 (docs/adr/0007-bm25-df-and-doc-record-schema-2.md:5): schema 2 'does every write under an index-level lock in a transaction'; spec 044 FR-016/FR-018 (specs/044-bm25-index/spec.md:162-164): df, N, totalLen consistent 'at every committed point'; FR-019 (:165) two writers never interleave; decisions.md HD-0701 working answer: serialize index modifications and publish a complete generation or unavailable, including crash.
entry.observed: Live (b-07-f0701-race): an Insert from a second process landed during a 3000-node Build; final N=3000/totalLen=12000 against 3001 doc records summing 12003 (TXT-I2 broken, the inserted doc searchable but uncounted); a concurrent reader saw N=1, schema 2 mid-build. Journal: Build 30008 records, none in a transaction; Insert one transaction. Model: m07-bm25-as-built-I2/-I5 (insert during build), m07-bm25-as-built-settle (Drop during Build leaves a header over no postings), m07-bm25-as-built-quiesced-crash (a stopped build then an Insert breaks I2 even with operators keeping writers apart); reviewed design m07-bm25-reviewed passes; controls caught.
entry.remedy: Per HD-0701: Build takes the write lock for its run, writes a shadow generation and publishes it in one step (or sets a building flag that writers refuse); Drop takes the lock; a crash leaves the old generation or an explicit unavailable state.
entry.notes: Upgrade's schema-1 path (Build or Drop during Upgrade) is covered by the model only: the pin's API cannot create a schema-1 index for a live run.

bugs_issues.title: Two plan shapes with one 32-bit checksum share one compiled class

entry.title: Two plan shapes with one 32-bit checksum share one compiled class
entry.intended: ADR-0014 (docs/adr/0014-native-plans-are-compiled-to-classes-at-run-time.md:19): 'A compiled class answers exactly as the interpreter does'; NAT-I3 (a read never runs code written for another plan shape); NAT-T5.16.
entry.observed: Live (b-09-f0901-collision): a birthday search in IRIS over label names of one length found two labels B09QXAYMSHXLZD / B09QWCSOJEBLDF whose plan shapes share $ZCRC(shape,7) = 1912394325 after 90195 candidates (0.23 s); hashes of the separately compiled shapes: {'B09QXAYMSHXLZD': ['1912394325'], 'B09QWCSOJEBLDF': ['1912394325']}. In job mode (one process) a read of the B09QWCSOJEBLDF shape (its build job compiling) then a read of the B09QXAYMSHXLZD shape left one entry, status ['ok']; the next B09QXAYMSHXLZD read answered [[2]] where the SQL path answers [[1]]; a shadow-mode engine raised NativeMismatch; another process's engine answered [[2]]: the B09QXAYMSHXLZD entry runs the class compiled from the B09QWCSOJEBLDF shape's lines (it counts B09QWCSOJEBLDF nodes), in every process. Model: m09-planc-as-built-collide-I3 (a read mid-walk runs the rebuilt class of the other shape), -binding (the entry of one shape marked ok for the class compiled from the other), -progress (two colliding shapes never both run compiled); reviewed per-shape names pass (m09-planc-reviewed); control m09-planc-control-shared-name caught.
entry.remedy: Name the class by a digest wide enough to rule out collisions (the SHA-256 Digest already computes) or a counter, keep the shape check, and have Build verify under its lock that the entry still holds the shape it compiled before marking it ok.
entry.notes: Labels, relationship types and property keys are caller-chosen, so a collision is constructible on demand (birthday search over ~10^5 names in seconds), not only the accident P-0901's odds describe; one caller's reads can thereby change the answers of another caller's queries of a colliding shape in the same namespace until a deploy, a DropAll or a stamp change.

bugs_issues.title: A cached personalized PageRank answer misses a start node written or removed without an edge

entry.title: A cached personalized PageRank answer misses a start node written or removed without an edge
entry.intended: ALG-B2.19 (a cached answer changes when a start node is added to the graph or removed from it); ALG-B16.11 (after any write a cached answer equals a fresh computation); ALG-I4.
entry.observed: Live (b-10-live-cache): kg_PERSONALIZED_PAGERANK(['b10_x']) answered {} before b10_x existed and the answer was cached (^IVG.AlgoCache(0,'ppr',...)); create_node('b10_x') with no edge wrote only nodes/rdf_props and moved no token; the same call then answered {} from the cache while a fresh run (after AlgoCache.InvalidateAll) answered {'b10_x': 1.0, 'b10_a': 0.0, 'b10_b': 0.0}. Refuted part: deleting the edgeless start node moved ^KG('__version') (7128 -> 7131 for a labelled node; edgeless 7125 -> 7127) because delete_node runs Graph.KG.Eraser.EraseNodeIds, whose InvalidateDerived bumps the token and kills ^IVG.AlgoCache (Eraser.cls:1038-1053); the next call answered {}, equal to a fresh run. Models: m10-cache-as-built-ppr (violation, linearizable property), m10-cache-reviewed-ppr (monotonic node token: pass), m10-cache-control-no-bump-on-create (caught).
entry.remedy: Put the node-set token in the PPR key (as global PageRank does since R313) or raise a node token on every node write and read it inside AlgoCache.Lookup; a live test that creates an edgeless start node after a cached call.
entry.notes: Only the 'written' half reproduces at the pin; the 'removed' half is refuted live (a node delete always raises the token and clears the cache). The global PageRank key (R313, COUNT(*):MAX(%ID)) is sound within the model's bounds only because deletes raise the token: m10-cache-control-silent-delete-pagerank shows the ABA it would otherwise admit (COUNT:MAX returns to an earlier value when the newest node is deleted).

bugs_issues.title: An adoption is not tied to the head it compared

entry.title: An adoption is not tied to the head it compared
entry.intended: LED-B1.20 (an adoption records only the unrecorded writes it was built from; nothing a later commit did); the history replays to the live store (spec 213 verify); decisions.md HD-1401 (verify needs a coherent cut across its reads).
entry.observed: Live AUDITB with a forced interleaving at a Python call boundary in the harness (replay.read_canonical wrapped; no product file changed): a commit of b11_a-B11T-b11_b (stmt 1, seq 2) landed after verify(adopt=True) had read the records up to its head and before it read the stores; the adoption revision (seq 3) recorded create_rel stmt 1 a second time, so LED-B1.20 is violated (b-11-live-f1103). verify() afterwards still answered equal (replay is idempotent on the statement id), so the 'history no longer replays' impact was not observed for this schedule. Double adoption by two concurrent re-enables was not reproduced live in 6 trials (one Enable always saw the other's state; b-11-live-f1103-reenable-race). Model: m11-adopt-as-built-commit and m11-adopt-as-built-two-enables violate LED-B1.20; m11-adopt-reviewed (adoption sends the verified head, re-verifies on stale head) passes; control m11-adopt-control-nocheck caught.
entry.remedy: Send the verified head as expected_head on the adoption and re-verify on StaleHeadError (or compute the adoption under the head lock on the server); re-read the state under the head lock in Enable so two re-enables cannot both answer adoption_needed.
entry.notes: The forced schedule is realizable by any concurrent commit during verify's reads (verify reads every record, then every live table).

bugs_issues.title: A graph erasure removes the statement entry of an edge a concurrent ledger commit creates

entry.title: A graph erasure removes the statement entry of an edge a concurrent ledger commit creates
entry.intended: No recorded live edge loses its statement entry (ERS-I3; ADR-0004: 'no live statement outlives its content' and the ledger's statement map tracks every live recorded edge). HD-1201 working answer: erase serializes with same-target commits.
entry.observed: Reproduced on the pin 8/8: EraseGraph takes no ledger head lock (Eraser.cls:47-261) and EraseLedgerFor (Eraser.cls:1117-1144) dirty-reads every statement entry; it killed the committer's ^IVG.Ledger("stmt",4001) and tuple after the commit wrote them; the edge u-R-v, its nodes and adjacency stayed live in G with no statement entry. Journal order is the oracle. With an edge in the graph the same race instead makes the erase fail with an FK error and roll back (8/8); with a short statement scan the eraser wins the race (8/8).
entry.remedy: Serialize graph erasure with ledger commits into the same graph (for example take the ledger head lock, or a per-graph lock both take, around the statement cleanup), or make the cleanup remove only statements whose edge rows the same transaction deleted.
entry.notes: Upgraded from model-only (original submission) to live. The next ledger operation touching the edge, and verify(), see an unrecorded live edge. Review-response reclassification (review R2-08 / R-11, condition 5; 2026-11-14): disposition changed from reproduced-live to intent-undecided. ERS-I3 (every live recorded edge keeps its statement entry) is the converse of what ADR-0004 states ('no live statement outlives its content': ERS-I2), so the ADR-0004 citation does not support it; spec 213's contracts (contracts/ledger-api.md, contracts/changeset.schema.json) state no statement-map completeness rule either (checked by this lane). The remaining basis is HD-1201, an Assumption (erase serializes with same-target commits; 'choice of lock is provisional'). Observed behaviour kept and still live 8/8: live-f1201-reproduced (journal order as oracle), live-erase-vs-commit-fk, live-erase-vs-commit-emptygraph. The overlap of an eraser with a writer of the same graph is recorded as the violated breadth premise P-A3 (TRUST.md), which does not depend on this intent. Conditional on HD-1201. Review-2 R2-11 (final): restored to reproduced-live. ADR-0004's Consequences clause ('no live statement outlives its content' and the statement map must track recorded live edges) makes the observed state a defect; only the remedy (which lock or protocol serializes erasure with commits, HD-1201) is undecided.

bugs_issues.title: Bolt BEGIN, COMMIT and ROLLBACK do nothing; every RUN commits at once

entry.title: Bolt BEGIN, COMMIT and ROLLBACK do nothing; every RUN commits at once
entry.intended: A Bolt explicit transaction is atomic: ROLLBACK discards the writes made since BEGIN (Bolt protocol, P-1612; API-B9.10 'A rollback should undo the writes made since the driver began its transaction').
entry.observed: Live (c16-s1-cypher-http): neo4j driver 6.4.1 began a transaction, ran CREATE c16:b1, rolled back; the node is still there (count 1). The journal shows the RUN's write committed in its own outermost IRIS transaction before ROLLBACK arrived. A managed transaction (execute_write) whose second statement fails keeps the first statement's node c16:b2. Source: BEGIN/COMMIT answer SUCCESS and ROLLBACK only clears pending rows (iris_vector_graph/bolt_server.py:500-510); RUN calls engine.execute_cypher, which commits (bolt_server.py:567-591).
entry.remedy: Run a Bolt transaction's RUNs inside one engine write transaction and commit/roll it back on COMMIT/ROLLBACK, or refuse BEGIN with a FAILURE that says explicit transactions are unsupported.
entry.model_hint: as-built: each RUN commits immediately; BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK are acknowledgements only (bolt_server.py:500-510, 580). A driver retry of a managed unit of work after a failure re-applies the committed statements. Reviewed (decisions.md HD-1603 policy applied to Bolt units): RUNs of a BEGIN..COMMIT unit become visible together at COMMIT; ROLLBACK leaves no effect; a retried unit applies once. Invariant: committed effects == effects of COMMITted units.
entry.notes: Driver retries make it worse: execute_write retries a unit after transient errors, re-running statements that already committed.

bugs_issues.title: The Neo4j HTTP commit route runs its statements one by one

entry.title: The Neo4j HTTP commit route runs its statements one by one
entry.intended: Neo4j's /db/neo4j/tx/commit is a begin-and-commit-in-one-request transaction: all statements or none (P-1612); API-B8.6.1.
entry.observed: Live (c16-s1-cypher-http): three statements (CREATE c16:t1; an unparsable line; CREATE c16:t3) answered 400 with one SyntaxError, and both c16:t1 and c16:t3 are committed — the third ran after the failure. Journal: two separate outermost commits on two different IRIS processes: the failed statement made _run_cypher reset the engine (closing the connection) and retry, so statement 3 ran on a new connection. Source: iris_vector_graph/cypher_api.py:379-410, :239-250.
entry.remedy: Run the statements in one engine transaction and roll back on the first error (Neo4j stops there), or document the route as non-atomic.
entry.model_hint: as-built: per-statement commit, later statements still run after an error (cypher_api.py:391-405). Reviewed: unit atomicity — the request's effects are all statements' or none; processing stops at the first error. Invariant: after a 4xx/5xx answer no statement effect of the request is committed.

entry.title: A failed server-loader bulk_create_nodes answers 'nothing written' while its first 1,000 nodes stay committed
entry.intended: docs/USER_GUIDE.md:238-241: with no caller transaction 'each write (... the bulk loaders ...) is a transaction of its own'; iris_vector_graph/_batch_check.py:68-80 (raise_if_missing: 'a writer raises it before its rollback, so nothing of the batch is written'); a GraphWriteError's text says what stayed written (4.7.0 row 14; the same rule F-0806 applies to Cypher).
entry.observed: Trace 03/bulk (tr-replay-03): bulk_create_nodes of 2,000 nodes on a from_connect engine (two 1,000-node chunks to Graph.KG.EdgeScan.BulkIngestNodesSQL on the engine's own Native API process, iris_vector_graph/_engine/nodes_edges.py:1715-1757), the last node carrying a 70,000-character property value (wider than rdf_props.val VARCHAR(64000), schema.py:415; _check_create_nodes checks id, label and key widths only, nodes_edges.py:243-262). The journal shows the loader process commit chunk 1 (1,000 node rows) in its own transaction, chunk 2 rolled back (TROLLBACK 1 after SQLCODE -104 'property blob of tr03bk_1999'), and the SQL fallback on the cursor's process rolled back; the call raised GraphWriteError 'bulk_create_nodes failed, nothing written: IRIS refused 1 property row(s) of the batch ...' and a later SELECT counted 1,000 committed nodes. Replayed through wrt_bulk_atomic (as built) the trace ends in Raised with committed = (chunk 1, not chunk 2), violating WRT-B3.19; the reviewed design diverges at the first chunk's commit.
entry.remedy: Run the loader chunks on the caller's process inside the WriteTxn (txn.native() in every case, the F-0305 fix), so a failed batch leaves nothing; until then, a failure after a committed chunk must say how many nodes stayed committed instead of 'nothing written'.
entry.notes: Same mechanism as F-0305 (chunks committed by another process); F-0305's recorded observation is a successful call whose partial state another process could see mid-call. This is the failure path: the end state is partial and the reply states the opposite. Found by the trace-replay lane (AUDITE).

entry.title: get_json_field_values pastes the field name into its SQL text, so a field name can change the statement
entry.intended: SQL text carries only constants and identifiers the code controls, values are bound (the product's own pattern elsewhere: _validate, sanitize_identifier; F-0815 for the same class of defect in Cypher); get_json_field_values(key, field) answers the field's values inside the key's blobs (iris_vector_graph/_engine/nodes_edges.py:916-930).
entry.observed: Live AUDITD (st-live-susp-json-field), scratch rows jf:1 'meta' = {"color": "red"} and jf:2 'private' = {"color": "blue"}: get_json_field_values('meta', 'color') answers ['red']; a field containing one quote makes the statement fail ('Incorrect number of parameters'); a crafted field ending in ... WHERE "key" <> ? AND (1 = 1 OR val LIKE ?) -- turns the statement into a read of every other key and answers ['blue'] from the 'private' row. The field is formatted into a string literal of the select list (nodes_edges.py:921-922) and into the LIKE pattern (:926). The query also has no graph predicate.
entry.remedy: Bind the field: build the marker with a parameter (SELECT $PIECE($PIECE(val, ?, 2), '"', 1) ... with the bound text '"' + field + '": "'), escape % and _ in the LIKE pattern with an ESCAPE clause, or validate field against a strict identifier pattern; add a graph predicate.
entry.notes: Only read-only crafted text was used; nothing was written. The statement runs with the caller's own SQL privileges, so the effect is reading rows or tables the caller's code did not ask for when field comes from an end user. No product caller of this public engine method was found.

bugs_issues.title: Racing create_edge calls on a new edge whose endpoint is new can all lose: some answer False ('already exists') and no edge is written

entry.title: Racing create_edge calls on a new edge whose endpoint is new can all lose: some answer False ('already exists') and no edge is written
entry.intended: create_edge answers False only if the edge already existed, a duplicate is never an error (iris_vector_graph/_engine/nodes_edges.py:1176-1186 docstring); when two writers race to create one edge, one adds it and the other answers False (WRT-B4.9, 03-writes.md:118; nodes_edges.py:1243-1245 'a concurrent writer won the race'); endpoint rows a concurrent writer got to first are not an error (nodes_edges.py:1123-1124).
entry.observed: Live AUDITD (st-live-keys-race-edge): four connections released together call create_edge('rx:1','R','rx:2') with rx:2 not yet a node. In 4 of 8 trials no call succeeds: two answer False and two raise GraphWriteError SQLCODE -121 (fk_edges_dest), and afterwards neither the edge nor rx:2 exists. With both endpoints present beforehand, 8 of 8 trials give one True, three False and one edge. Reading of the code: a racer that meets another racer's uncommitted endpoint row skips its own insert (nodes_edges.py:1123-1124), its edge insert then fails the FK or meets another racer's uncommitted edge row, and -119 from an uncommitted row that later rolls back is answered as a duplicate (nodes_edges.py:1243-1245, 1251-1255).
entry.remedy: Treat -119/-121 met against another writer's uncommitted row as 'retry' rather than 'duplicate': wait on the row (a SQL lock on the key, e.g. LOCK of the (graph, s, p, o) tuple before the probe) and re-probe after it commits or rolls back; answer False only when a committed edge is found.
entry.notes: A caller that receives False has no reason to retry, so the write is lost. The same race shape (several -119/-121/-110 errors, nothing written) was seen for bulk_create_nodes, store_node, Cypher MERGE of a new path and concurrent reify_edge (st-live-keys); those raise errors rather than answer success, so callers can retry.

bugs_issues.title: The bulk loader writes duplicate node, label, property and edge keys: an id twice in one batch, a load with skip_existing=False, or two loaders at once

entry.title: The bulk loader writes duplicate node, label, property and edge keys: an id twice in one batch, a load with skip_existing=False, or two loaders at once
entry.intended: Graph_KG.nodes is keyed by (node_id, graph_id), rdf_labels by (graph_id, s, label), rdf_props by (graph_id, s, key) and rdf_edges by (s, p, o_id, graph_id, ekey) (iris_vector_graph/schema.py:35-44, 396-419). BulkLoader writes %NOINDEX %NOCHECK, which skips those checks (P-0304), and relies on its own scans to keep them: 'Without the hint every existence check here believes the previous bulk load never happened, and %NOCHECK means the second copy lands without complaint' (iris_vector_graph/bulk_loader.py:182-199); load_edges dedupes its input in memory (bulk_loader.py:420-427).
entry.observed: Live AUDITD (st-live-keys): load_nodes([('kb:1', ...), ('kb:1', ...)]) answers nodes 2, labels 2, props 4 and leaves two node rows, two label rows and two rows per property key for (default graph, kb:1); get_node('kb:1') answers labels ['A', 'A']. load_nodes and load_edges run a second time with skip_existing=False duplicate the node, label, prop and edge keys. Two loaders of the same 50 ids started together each write all 50 nodes. In every case rebuild_all_indices answers True for all four classes and the duplicates stay; the load answers report no error.
entry.remedy: Deduplicate node ids (and labels/properties per node) in the batch as load_edges does; refuse skip_existing=False under %NOCHECK or drop %NOCHECK for the key-carrying inserts; serialise loaders of one graph (a lock on the graph) and check the declared keys before %BuildIndices, failing the load on a duplicate.
entry.notes: The default path (skip_existing=True, one loader, distinct ids) keeps the keys. The duplicates are invisible to index reads that pick one row and visible to scans and to get_node's label list.

bugs_issues.title: BulkLoader.load_edges' INSERT %NOINDEX %NOCHECK lets a graph whose mode is off hold two rows of one triple at the same edge key, and the index rebuild accepts them

entry.title: BulkLoader.load_edges' INSERT %NOINDEX %NOCHECK lets a graph whose mode is off hold two rows of one triple at the same edge key, and the index rebuild accepts them
entry.intended: specs/234-multigraph-parallel-edges/spec.md:32-35, 225-226 and GID-I4.10 (experiment/playbook-uplift/ontology: a graph whose mode is off never holds parallel edges, whatever engine or path writes to it); iris_vector_graph/schema.py:34-44 (u_spo_graph_ekey UNIQUE (s, p, o_id, graph_id, ekey)); iris_vector_graph/bulk_loader.py:396 (skip_existing 'avoids UNIQUE violations').
entry.observed: Live in AUDITB (ws-live-ba-noindex-parallel), default graph, mode off: BulkLoader.load_edges([('wsgp|a','R','wsgp|b',None)]) with its default use_noindex=True wrote one row at ekey 0 that the indexes do not hold; engine.create_edge of the same triple returned True and wrote a second row, also at ekey 0 (its guard and the unique key read the index); BulkLoader.rebuild_all_indices answered True for every index with both rows of key (wsgp|a, R, wsgp|b, '', 0) in place. Two load_edges calls with skip_existing=False wrote two rows of another triple, both ekey 0, and the rebuild again answered True.
entry.remedy: Do not combine %NOCHECK with %NOINDEX for rdf_edges (or check the triple against every row with a %NOINDEX-aware read and within the batch whatever skip_existing says), and rebuild the indices before load_edges returns; validate the unique key when rebuilding it.
entry.notes: Same root as F-C1250 and F-C1351 (rows the indexes do not hold until rebuild_all_indices). Census writer pairs: GID-I4.10 x BulkLoader.load_edges / load_networkx (models/breadth-a/writesets.json). Part (b), duplicate edge keys from two load_edges(skip_existing=False) calls, is the same behaviour as F-C0349 (zz-structural.json, st-live-keys); part (a), a default load followed by create_edge, is new here.

bugs_issues.title: A ledger relationship whose qualifiers hold temporal=1 is deleted as a temporal edge's derived row, and its statement stays live

entry.title: A ledger relationship whose qualifiers hold temporal=1 is deleted as a temporal edge's derived row, and its statement stays live
entry.intended: docs/adr/0009-a-temporal-edge-implies-a-structural-edge.md:38-42 ('A row an explicit write asserted is unmarked and outlives the purge of its timestamps'); iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Adjacency.cls:619-621 (the row is deleted only while it carries the temporal marker, 'so an edge created explicitly outlives its temporal edges'); INV-stmt / ERS-I2 (no live statement without its row, experiment/playbook-uplift/ontology/12-erasure.md:42).
entry.observed: Live in AUDITB (ws-live-stmt-collision, ws-live-stmt-purge). The ledger accepts any qualifier key but id and __graph (LedgerApply.cls:68-71) and stores values as strings (QualsJson, LedgerApply.cls:420-434), so create_relationship(..., qualifiers={'temporal': 1}) is stored {"temporal":"1"}; Adjacency.IsTemporalMarked (736-748) tests %Get("temporal") = 1, which "1" satisfies, while the ledger's own adoption test is = "true" (LedgerApply.cls:469). (a) A temporal edge on the same triple and engine.delete_edge_temporal: TemporalIndex.DeleteTemporalEdge -> RetractTemporalRow deleted the ledger's row; (b) set_temporal_structural('RD', False) and drop_temporal_structural_rows('RD'): TemporalPolicy.DropRows (pass 2 parses with IsTemporalMarked) deleted it and retired its 2 recorded endpoint nodes; (c) engine.purge_before(2000) after a temporal edge at ts 1000: RetractTemporalRows' %STARTSWITH test misses and its fallback RetractTemporalRow (Adjacency.cls:677-679) deleted it. Each time the statement (^IVG.Ledger("stmt", id), closed seq empty) and its tuple index entry stay live with no row; verify() went equal -> diverges (unrecorded_writes).
entry.remedy: Mark derived rows with something a governed relationship cannot carry (a reserved qualifier key the ledger and every writer refuse, or a separate column), and make every marker test use the same predicate; or have the temporal retraction refuse a row that has a live statement.
entry.notes: A user qualifier named 'temporal' is unusual but unrestricted; the same row is also adopted (qualifiers set to NULL) by bulk_create_edges' _ADOPT_TEMPORAL_ROW_SQL if it matches _TEMPORAL_MARKED_ROW. Same predicate defect as F-0505 (reproduced-live: an explicit edge with temporal:1 is deleted by the temporal delete); F-C0450 adds the ledger-statement consequence and the DropRows and purge paths.

bugs_issues.title: An index built under the stopword name makes index-structure words stopwords in every BM25 index

entry.title: An index built under the stopword name makes index-structure words stopwords in every BM25 index
entry.intended: TXT-D1 (a stopword is one of 77 common English words); HD-0704 (reserve the stopword name).
entry.observed: Live (b-07-f0706): after bm25_build('__stop__', ['name'], graph='b07g1') the words 'doc', 'tf', 'len' (and 'cfg', 'df') are stopwords for every index in the namespace: a rebuild of index b07w drops them (searches for each answer [] where they answered b07_w1 before) because Tokenize's stopword test $Data(^BM25Idx("__stop__", tok)) (BM25Index.cls:83) is true for the index's own subscripts. The effect lasts until the __stop__ index is dropped (which also deletes the stopword list until the next tokenize).
entry.remedy: Refuse the name (HD-0704) or move the stopword list to its own global.
entry.notes: Same root cause as F-0706 (the stopword list shares the index key space); distinct impact: silent wrong answers in other indexes.

bugs_issues.title: bm25_search rewrites document ids: its leading-dot patch runs over the whole answer, so an id holding ':.5', ',.7' or '[.9' comes back as ':0.5', ',0.7', '[0.9'

entry.title: bm25_search rewrites document ids: its leading-dot patch runs over the whole answer, so an id holding ':.5', ',.7' or '[.9' comes back as ':0.5', ',0.7', '[0.9'
entry.intended: TXT-B2 (search returns each best document with its node id and score); TXT-B2.13 (each id and score in the answer is valid JSON, ids included); CHANGELOG.md:463-467 (4.6.3: 'Search answers keep a node id with a quote or a backslash', each answer escaped as RFC 8259 asks); docs/USER_GUIDE.md:859-866 (bm25_search and CALL ivg.bm25.search answer the same nodes); tests/e2e/test_463_search_id_escaping_e2e.py:57-71 asserts the Python and Cypher answers agree id for id.
entry.observed: Live (rx-dec-live-07, case 'ids containing ...'): graph rxdg, nodes rxd:a, rxd:.5x, rxd,.7y, rxd[.9z, rxd:b with the word zebra, index rxdidx. Graph.KG.BM25Index.Search's raw answer is valid JSON with the ids exactly as stored and every score already written with a leading 0 (no '"score":.' in the wire); bm25_search answered ('rxd:0.5x', ...), ('rxd,0.7y', ...), ('rxd[0.9z', ...) for 3 of the 5 rows, and bm25_search(report=True) the same; CALL ivg.bm25.search (JSON_TABLE over the same wire) answered the ids unchanged. Cause: _parse applies re.sub(r'(?<=[:\[,])(\.\d)', r'0\1', raw) to the whole JSON text, string values included (iris_vector_graph/_engine/vector.py:1817-1819); the patch is redundant since BM25Index.SearchCore writes the leading 0 itself (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/BM25Index.cls:361-365). The static check lists the pattern as not token-aware (rx-dec-map).
entry.remedy: Drop the text patch (the server already writes a leading 0), or apply it to number tokens only by parsing with json.loads(parse_float=...) after a token-aware scan; add an id with ':.5' to the 4.6.3 id-escaping test.
entry.notes: An altered id can name another existing node (rxd:0.5x) or none; the Cypher path is unaffected. The number fix the patch guards (TXT-B2.13, '.5' written as '0.5' since 4.2) is done server-side.

bugs_issues.title: One token longer than the subscript limit in any document makes bm25_build fail after it has emptied the index, and searches then answer nothing

entry.title: One token longer than the subscript limit in any document makes bm25_build fail after it has emptied the index, and searches then answer nothing
entry.intended: A refused command leaves every store as it was (SYS-I3, TXT-X2 in experiment/playbook-uplift/ontology/07-text-search.md; cited by F-0704); Build indexes every node of the graph over the named properties (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/BM25Index.cls:97-175).
entry.observed: Live AUDITD (st-live-cap-bm25): with one document holding a 600- or 2,000-character token (or a 300-character token in a document whose id has 256 characters), bm25_build raises 'RuntimeError: <THROW>' and leaves the index without documents; rebuilding a good 5-document index after one such node is added destroys it the same way, and bm25_search for any ordinary term then answers [] without error. Build kills ^BM25Idx(name) first (BM25Index.cls:99) and Tokenize tests each token with $Data(^BM25Idx("__stop__", tok)) (:83), which raises <SUBSCRIPT> for a long token; bm25_insert and bm25_search with such a token raise <SUBSCRIPT> and leave the index unchanged. Tokens of 200 and 400 characters index normally.
entry.remedy: Skip or truncate tokens longer than a fixed length in Tokenize (before any subscript use), and build into a temporary name that replaces the old index only on success (as F-0704's remedy); report the document that failed.
entry.notes: Same kill-before-build root as F-0704 (a refused index-handle build), reached here by data rather than by a bad argument: a URL, hash or sequence of a few hundred characters anywhere in the graph makes the graph's BM25 index unbuildable.

bugs_issues.title: MERGE ... ON CREATE SET r = a gives every merged relationship the first row's properties

entry.title: MERGE ... ON CREATE SET r = a gives every merged relationship the first row's properties
entry.intended: openCypher: MERGE runs once per incoming row; `SET r = a` copies that row's node a onto that row's relationship (CYP-B6.8 per-row MERGE semantics); gate §3.4 storage-order.
entry.observed: Live (b-08-live-storage-order): `MATCH (a:B08PP), (t:B08TT {id:'b08_tt'}) MERGE (a)-[r:B08MR3]->(t) ON CREATE SET r = a` with a = b08_p1 {city:'ca', pop:1} and b08_p2 {city:'cb', pop:2} created two relationships whose qualifiers were both {id:'b08_p1', city:'ca', pop:'1'}. The translator copies `(SELECT TOP 1 a.node_id FROM <preceding rows>)` (translator.py:12362-12395) with no ORDER BY and applies one UPDATE to every merged relationship, so the stored values come from whichever row storage order puts first.
entry.remedy: Correlate the copied node with each relationship's own row (per-row UPDATE through the row-bound MERGE plan, or a correlated subquery on the relationship's source/target), or refuse `SET r = a` when the preceding clauses bind more than one row; live test with two rows.
entry.notes: The sibling path `_merge_action_value_sql` (translator.py:11123-11190, same TOP 1 of the preceding rows) was not reached: `MATCH (p) MERGE (c:B08CT {name: p.city}) ON CREATE SET c.pop = p.pop` was refused with <ARGUMENT ERROR> (cf. F-0809). CYP-X6.8.6 refuses an edge's ON CREATE value read from another variable's property, not a whole-node copy.

bugs_issues.title: A Cypher CREATE or MERGE with literal or parameter endpoint ids drops a parameter-bound relationship property without an error

entry.title: A Cypher CREATE or MERGE with literal or parameter endpoint ids drops a parameter-bound relationship property without an error
entry.intended: docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md:89-95: 'A literal (a list or a map too), a parameter and a WITH's column are stored'; iris_vector_graph/cypher/translator.py:507-512 (_refuse_unstorable_rel_props: a parameter is stored, anything it cannot store is refused before writing).
entry.observed: Live AUDITD (st-live-cypher-relprop, found by st-live-cap-values): CREATE (a:L {id: 'a2'})-[:R {q: $v}]->(b:L {id: 'b2'}), the same with $s/$o endpoint ids, with a number parameter, and MERGE (a:L {id: 'a4'})-[:R {q: $v}]->(b:L {id: 'b4'}) each answer no error and create the edge with no q (rdf_edges.qualifiers empty; r.q null). The same parameter between MATCHed endpoints and a literal q are stored. The literal-endpoint path (translator.py:10213-10222) resolves an ast.Literal or a FOREACH binding only, so a parameter resolves to None and is dropped as a null property (:10228).
entry.remedy: Resolve parameters (context.input_params) in the literal-endpoint path as _rel_literal_props does, or route such patterns through _rel_literal_props; refuse any property the writer cannot store instead of dropping it.
entry.notes: Not a capacity effect: the property is dropped at every size (10 characters included). Found by the capacity probe's read-back oracle.

bugs_issues.title: A build marks whatever entry its hash holds as ok, so one shape's entry can run another shape's class for good

entry.title: A build marks whatever entry its hash holds as ok, so one shape's entry can run another shape's class for good
entry.intended: NAT-T5.16 (a ready entry runs only the class written for its own shape) and NAT-I3; ADR-0014:19.
entry.observed: Live (b-09-f0901-collision): a birthday search in IRIS over label names of one length found two labels B09QXAYMSHXLZD / B09QWCSOJEBLDF whose plan shapes share $ZCRC(shape,7) = 1912394325 after 90195 candidates (0.23 s); hashes of the separately compiled shapes: {'B09QXAYMSHXLZD': ['1912394325'], 'B09QWCSOJEBLDF': ['1912394325']}. In job mode (one process) a read of the B09QWCSOJEBLDF shape (its build job compiling) then a read of the B09QXAYMSHXLZD shape left one entry, status ['ok']; the next B09QXAYMSHXLZD read answered [[2]] where the SQL path answers [[1]]; a shadow-mode engine raised NativeMismatch; another process's engine answered [[2]]: the B09QXAYMSHXLZD entry runs the class compiled from the B09QWCSOJEBLDF shape's lines (it counts B09QWCSOJEBLDF nodes), in every process. Model: m09-planc-as-built-collide-I3 (a read mid-walk runs the rebuilt class of the other shape), -binding (the entry of one shape marked ok for the class compiled from the other), -progress (two colliding shapes never both run compiled); reviewed per-shape names pass (m09-planc-reviewed); control m09-planc-control-shared-name caught.
entry.remedy: Under its lock, Build writes the entry only if it still holds the shape (or digest) it compiled; otherwise it deletes the class and leaves the entry.
entry.notes: Root cause shared with F-0901 (two shapes on one 32-bit name) but a distinct mechanism: F-0901 describes a transient mid-walk race and overwrite churn; here the wrong binding persists across reads and processes until a deploy, a DropAll or a stamp change. The R311 digest check (:175-182) compares only the lines it merged, before compiling, and does not prevent it.

bugs_issues.title: A plain SQL INSERT into Graph_KG.ledger_revisions is accepted, and a row planted at head+1 made the next ledger commit fail

entry.title: A plain SQL INSERT into Graph_KG.ledger_revisions is accepted, and a row planted at head+1 made the next ledger commit fail
entry.intended: iris_src/src/Graph/KG/LedgerRevision.cls:1-5 ('one immutable row per committed revision ... Written only by Graph.KG.Ledger.Commit inside the commit transaction'; UPDATE and DELETE are rejected, FR-023).
entry.observed: Live in AUDITB (ws-live-sql-insert-wedge): with head seq 3, an SQL INSERT of a row with seq 4 and every required column was accepted (the table has UPDATE and DELETE triggers, no INSERT trigger); the next engine.ledger.commit (the only one attempted after the INSERT) failed LedgerInconsistencyError 'revision row save failed: ERROR #5805: ID key not unique ... ^Graph.KG.LedgerRevisionD(4) exists'; verify() still answered equal. An INSERT of an existing seq is refused (SeqIdx) and UPDATE is refused (trigger) (ws-live-sql-guard), so the INSERT cannot rewrite history; it blocks the ledger.
entry.remedy: Add an INSERT trigger (or %OnBeforeSave check) that refuses a row outside Ledger.Commit's transaction, as for UPDATE and DELETE; and have verify() report a revision row with no records.
entry.notes: The census's '<any SQL client>::INSERT INTO Graph_KG.ledger_revisions' writer (review R-02's inferred revision-insert wedge, not probed before). Any SQL user with INSERT on the table can do this; whether later commits keep failing was not observed (one commit was attempted); F-1801's restore reaches the same ID-key collision, and its record states the ledger 'can never commit again' from the model (Ledger.cls:530-556).

bugs_issues.title: A bounded redaction (max_batches) restarts its scan at the first record and may never finish

entry.title: A bounded redaction (max_batches) restarts its scan at the first record and may never finish
entry.intended: LedgerRedact.cls:178-180: 'pMaxBatches > 0 stops after that many batches and leaves the run in progress; running the same target again resumes it.' RED-B8 (a stopped run resumes); spec 256 SC-003 (batching).
entry.observed: Live on the pin: 60 calls with batch 1 and max_batches 1 each re-scanned the first 20 records (batch x SCANFACTOR cap, :306-310) from the start (:213), tombstoned nothing and returned complete=false; 9 target records remained. The same world completes with max_batches 0. Model: core M2 paced-resume progress mutant and AG EF failure.
entry.remedy: Persist the scan cursor with the marker (or start each call after the last tombstoned position) so a resumed call continues where the previous one stopped.
entry.notes: With the default batch 2000 the cap is 40,000 records: a ledger with more non-target records before the target's never progresses under max_batches. The core proofs lane's reviewed model keeps the cursor across stops for this reason (model-level).

bugs_issues.title: IVG's own snapshot archives keep an erased and redacted tenant, the receipt does not name them, and a restore brings the tenant back

entry.title: IVG's own snapshot archives keep an erased and redacted tenant, the receipt does not name them, and a restore brings the tenant back
entry.intended: specs/256-ledger-tenant-redaction/spec.md:42-44 (US1: afterwards 'no record, revision field or index reachable through IVG holds the tenant's entity ids, attribute values or messages'; the receipt says 'what stayed out of reach'); spec.md:127-128 (FR-008: the receipt states what stays out of reach); docs/adr/0013-redaction-removes-content-from-history.md:47-48 ('Together they cover everything IVG can reach'; out of reach: export_reconstruction files, journals, backups); iris_src/src/Graph/KG/LedgerRedact.cls:504-508 (the receipt's out_of_reach: exactly those three).
entry.observed: Live in AUDITA (fu-r01a-snapshot-copies): tenant fu1|x committed through the ledger with a secret property, message, source, correlation id and idempotency key; engine.save_snapshot (the call POST /admin/snapshot makes with $IVG_SNAPSHOT_DIR or the temp folder, iris_vector_graph/cypher_api.py:668-678) taken before the erase, after the erase and after the redaction; delete_nodes_by_prefix + ledger.redact(None, prefix='fu1') complete, verify() equal, and the SC-001 scan of ^IVG.Ledger and Graph_KG.ledger_* finds none of the six tenant tokens. The pre-erase archive holds the tenant in sql/Graph_KG_nodes, rdf_labels, rdf_props, globals/IVG.Ledger (records, idempotency binding) and globals/Graph.KG.LedgerRevisionD (message, source, correlation id, idempotency key); the after-erase archive holds the whole history; the after-redaction archive holds none. The receipt's out_of_reach names exports, journals and backups only. restore_snapshot of the pre-erase archive (the replacing default) put back the node, the property secret='fu1-sensitive-7f3a', the records and the revision row's message, correlation id and idempotency key; the SC-001 scan is non-zero again, and the idempotency binding the redaction moved to idemRedacted is live again.
entry.remedy: Name IVG's own archives (save_snapshot files, including those POST /admin/snapshot writes to $IVG_SNAPSHOT_DIR or the temp folder) in the receipt's out_of_reach and in ADR-0013's reach statement; optionally refuse or warn on restoring an archive older than a completed redaction (HD-1801's re-apply of live redactions) and give the HTTP snapshot a retention rule.
entry.notes: F-1801 records what a restore does to the ledger; this finding records the archives as copies of the tenant that IVG itself writes (on demand, by any API-key holder through POST /admin/snapshot, with no retention or deletion) and that the receipt and ADR-0013 leave out. Severity S2 (a receipt that understates what IVG holds); S1 if an operator relies on the receipt as an erasure statement. The archives here have mode 0600 because this probe ran with umask 077; the product sets no mode (snapshot.py:1035).

bugs_issues.title: A writer that keeps the target live holds a redaction open indefinitely, and while it is open every tenant's record readers, verify() and other redactions are refused

entry.title: A writer that keeps the target live holds a redaction open indefinitely, and while it is open every tenant's record readers, verify() and other redactions are refused
entry.intended: docs/adr/0013-redaction-removes-content-from-history.md:18 (Batches: while the marker exists 'a commit with a record in the target is refused'; 'Re-running the same redaction resumes it'); specs/256-ledger-tenant-redaction/spec.md:156 (Decision 3), :125 (FR-006), :148 (SC-004: other tenants' verify() result unchanged); iris_vector_graph/ledger/client.py:633-660 (redact docstring: calling again resumes the run).
entry.observed: Live in AUDITA (fu-r03-marker-held-open, two connections): tenant fa3 erased, a bounded run (batch 1, max_batches 1) left the marker. engine.create_node('fa3|zombie') on a non-strict ledger was accepted (no non-ledger writer reads the marker), while a ledger commit into fa3 was refused. Running the redaction again was refused at the entry liveness check ('still holds 4 live row(s)', LedgerRedact.cls:207-211). A run that passed the entry check while a second connection held the head lock tombstoned every remaining fa3 record, and after a bypass write during the wait Final refused ('became live again', :395-396); the marker stayed after every refusal. While it existed, tenant fb3's get_revision, diff and reconstruct raised RedactionInProgressError, verify() returned redaction_in_progress, and redact(None, prefix='fc3') of an erased tenant was refused redaction_in_progress; history() was not refused and returned the half-done state; an fb3 ledger commit succeeded. Only erasing fa3 again and re-running cleared it. The marker is removed only by Final (LedgerRedact.cls:439) and PurgeAll (Ledger.cls:242-248); there is no abandon call.
entry.remedy: Either make the marker binding on every writer of the content tables (the non-ledger write paths, Cypher updating clauses, POST /admin/load and the temporal mirror refuse a write into the marked target), or scope the readers' refusal to the marked target and add an operator abandon/rollback for a run that cannot finish; state 'no writer makes a marked target live' as a progress premise (P-C02).
entry.notes: Availability and cross-tenant impact: one writer that keeps re-creating a row of the target (careless or with the single shared API key, review R-03) blocks every tenant's ledger record readers, verify() and redactions for as long as it writes. Whether non-ledger writers must honour the marker is not settled by any source (ADR-0013 names only commits): the refusal-of-everyone part is as designed, its unbounded duration is not. The core models record this as 'AG EF still holds: erase again' under the premise that writers become quiet (models/core/MODELS.md:302, 310). Strict mode (client-side, HD-1103) would refuse engine.create_node but not POST /admin/load (import_graph_ndjson is checked only in strict mode) or temporal writes with a graph in non-strict mode.

bugs_issues.title: get_reifications reads the reifier's properties from every graph

entry.title: get_reifications reads the reifier's properties from every graph
entry.intended: get_reifications returns the reifiers of rdf_edges row edge_id with their properties (iris_vector_graph/_engine/schema.py:3335-3339); a reifier node is an ordinary node of one graph (15-integrations.md INT-D19, INT-E1; reify_edge writes it in the default graph, INT-E1.6 / F-1502), and since spec 227 a node id is unique per graph, not per namespace (iris_vector_graph/schema.py:383-391); content of one graph never shows up in an answer about another graph (00-system.md SYS-I2).
entry.observed: Live AUDITD (st-live-reads-b, non-interference oracle with self-test st-control-reads-selftest): default-graph edge a-R-b reified as rf1 with props {p: '1'}; adding a node rf1 in named graph stg2 with props {p: '2', q: 'x'} (and a reification of another edge) changed get_reifications(edge a-R-b) from [{reifier_id: rf1, properties: {id: rf1, p: '1'}}] to [{reifier_id: rf1, properties: {id: rf1, p: '2', q: 'x'}}]: another graph's property rows of the same id are joined in and overwrite the reifier's own. The query joins rdf_props on the id alone: LEFT JOIN rdf_props p ON p.s = r.reifier_id (schema.py:3343-3346), with no graph_id condition.
entry.remedy: Join the reifier's properties in the reifier node's graph (the graph reify_edge wrote it in, or the edge's graph once F-1502 is fixed): add the graph_id condition to the rdf_props join, e.g. through the nodes row of the reifier.
entry.notes: Distinct from F-1502 (where the reifier is written) and F-1503 (delete_reification deletes every graph's rows): this is the reader. A named graph that happens to hold a node with the reifier's id (another tenant's data) changes the answer about a default-graph edge.

bugs_issues.title: A finished Bolt session never gives back its IRIS connection

entry.title: A finished Bolt session never gives back its IRIS connection
entry.intended: API-T8.3 says each Bolt session opens its own IRIS connection; P-1609: each connection counts against the instance's connection/licence limit (8 on this Community container), so a session must release it.
entry.observed: Live (c16-s2-bolt-sessions): three sequential Bolt sessions (driver closed each, GOODBYE sent) left three new AUDITC IRIS processes alive 20 s later; they disappeared only when the server process stopped. Source: the session builds its engine lazily (iris_vector_graph/bolt_server.py:391-394) and its run() finally-blocks close only the socket (bolt_server.py:404, :423 WebSocket; :940, :957 TCP), never self._engine.conn.
entry.remedy: Close the session's engine connection when the session ends (finally block), or share a bounded pool.
entry.notes: On Community a handful of Bolt sessions exhaust IRIS connections for every client of the instance; the refused connection then reaches the driver as Neo.ClientError.Statement.SyntaxError (F-C1602).

bugs_issues.title: Bolt listens on every interface unless the server is started by `ivg server start`

entry.title: Bolt listens on every interface unless the server is started by `ivg server start`
entry.intended: docs/ADMIN_API.md:26-28: the Bolt listener 'listens on the address --host names, or on BOLT_TCP_HOST'; API-T9.1; HD-1705 working answer: local-only or explicit opt-in for unauthenticated external binding.
entry.observed: Live (c16-s6-status-maps): `uvicorn iris_vector_graph.cypher_api:app --host 127.0.0.1` served HTTP on 127.0.0.1:18617 and the Bolt listener on 0.0.0.0:18618. Source: cypher_api.py:51 defaults BOLT_TCP_HOST to 0.0.0.0; only the CLI sets it from --host (cli.py:429); the documented `python -m iris_vector_graph.cypher_api` binds HTTP 0.0.0.0:8000 and Bolt 0.0.0.0:7687 (cypher_api.py:779; ADMIN_API.md:22).
