bugs_issues.title: The Cypher HTTP server runs a query again after any failure, writes included

entry.title: The Cypher HTTP server runs a query again after any failure, writes included
entry.intended: decisions.md HD-1603 (working answer): retry only a read, a write known not to have run, or a write with a verified idempotency key; an ambiguous commit outcome stays unknown.
entry.observed: Live (c16-s4-server-retry, fault injection of a lost acknowledgement after the engine's commit, through the real FastAPI app on AUDITC): SET n.counter = n.counter + 1 — one request moved the counter from 1 to 3 and answered 200; CREATE without a key — after the control run made 1 C16R2 node, ONE faulted request brought the total to 3 (control total 1); CREATE with an id answered 200 {'columns': ['id'], 'rowCount': 1, 'rows': [['c16:r3']], 'status': 'OK'}. c16-s1 also shows a plain parse error triggering the reset-and-retry (two IRIS processes for one /db/neo4j/tx/commit). Source: _run_cypher retries once after any exception, resetting the engine (iris_vector_graph/cypher_api.py:239-250); every Cypher route uses it.
entry.remedy: Retry only reads or errors raised before the statement ran (connection refused at connect); otherwise return an unknown-outcome error; or carry an idempotency key end to end. Combine with the SDK retry (HD-1702, module 17) as one protocol.
entry.model_hint: as-built: on any exception after execute_cypher (including after the engine's commit) the server resets the connection and re-executes the same query (cypher_api.py:241-250). Reviewed (HD-1603): re-execute only if the first attempt is known not to have committed or the query is a read; an ambiguous outcome is reported as unknown. Invariant: one client request applies its write at most once. Combined with the SDK's own POST retry (sdk.py, HD-1702) the as-built protocol can apply one logical write up to 4 times.
entry.notes: The fault is a wrapper around engine.execute_cypher in the test process only (no product change); it models a connection lost after the server-side commit. Model: cmc-retry-as-built-once's shortest trace is the server re-running a committed write whose reply was lost; cmc-retry-as-built-honest: the client is told 'failed' for an applied write. The client half (SDK POST retry) is module 17's F-C1703.

bugs_issues.title: One HTTP client call can create a write twice (client resend after a late reply; server re-run after an exception)

entry.title: One HTTP client call can create a write twice (client resend after a late reply; server re-run after an exception)
entry.intended: decisions.md HD-1702 / HD-1603 (working): after an ambiguous outcome retry only a read, a write known not to have run, or one with a verified idempotency key; treat client and server retries as one protocol.
entry.observed: Live (c17-live-server): IVGClient(timeout=2 s, max_retries=3) through a proxy that held the first reply 4 s sent one CREATE (n:C17Dup {marker}); the proxy saw 2 requests, the client answered {'rows': [['c17dup-1794613789']]}, and AUDITC holds 2 nodes with that marker. Source: sdk.py:209-228 resends a POST after TimeoutException/ConnectError/5xx whatever the query; IVGServerError.is_retryable is any 5xx (sdk.py:41-42); cypher_api.py:250-268 re-runs execute_cypher on a fresh connection after any exception. Model: cmc-retry-as-built-once (expected-violation), cmc-retry-as-built-honest (expected-violation: a definite failure reported for an applied write), cmc-retry-reviewed (pass), controls cmc-retry-ctl-client/-server.
entry.remedy: Retry only reads or writes known not to have run (connect error before send); report an unknown outcome for an ambiguous write; or carry an end-to-end idempotency key (the ledger's retry key) through /api/cypher.
entry.notes: Intent status: HD-1702/HD-1603 are working assumptions (decisions.md), not maintainer decisions; the duplicate is observed behaviour either way. Shared with module 16 (server half).

bugs_issues.title: IRISGraphStore.query_nodes(limit=n) kills the calling Python process (SIGSEGV) on IRIS Community 2026.1 with the locked driver

entry.title: IRISGraphStore.query_nodes(limit=n) kills the calling Python process (SIGSEGV) on IRIS Community 2026.1 with the locked driver
entry.intended: A public store method either answers or raises (store_protocol.py:10-11); the product knows FETCH FIRST is hazardous for this driver/engine family and avoids it elsewhere (iris_vector_graph/engine.py:725-739 _fetch_first_unsafe and its subprocess probe :772-830; docs/iris-sql-quirks.md:47-62; the in-line comment iris_sql_store.py:1177-1178 records a segfault on FETCH FIRST ? ROWS ONLY on ARM64).
entry.observed: Live (st-live-so-confirm P17, AUDITD, IRIS 2026.1 Community build 234U, intersystems_irispython 5.3.2, x86_64): a child process that calls engine._store.query_nodes(limit=2) prints its start mark and exits with return code -11 (SIGSEGV) before any answer, in both insertion orders; the first attempt inside the permutation harness ended the harness with 'dumped core'. The statement is SELECT node_id FROM Graph_KG.nodes FETCH FIRST 2 ROWS ONLY (iris_vector_graph/stores/iris_sql_store.py:1179-1180), sent without consulting _fetch_first_unsafe. Attribution control (st-live-so-17b): the same statement from a harness cursor also exits -11, the TOP spelling answers: the crash is the engine/driver's behaviour on this statement, which the adapter sends without the engine's own _fetch_first_unsafe check.
entry.remedy: Use TOP n (as the translator does for joins and the engine does when _fetch_first_unsafe is set) or consult _fetch_first_unsafe in the adapter; a test that runs query_nodes(limit=n) on the supported driver.
entry.notes: The structural lane tested driver 5.3.2 (the pin's uv.lock) only; the contract-2 lane's runs merged below add the 5.4.0 control (no crash). A segfault is uncatchable in-process: every caller of the adapter (LazyKG, the store protocol's users) loses the process. Merged (orchestrator, steer 8): the contract-2 lane filed the same defect independently as F-C1720 and added the cause and a driver control: the call sends FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY (iris_sql_store.py:1162-1181) without consulting the product's own FETCH FIRST guard (engine.py:726-840); every FETCH FIRST form crashes driver 5.3.2 (env2-fetchfirst-probe) and none crashes 5.4.0 (env2-fetchfirst-probe-d540, env2-fc1720-query-nodes-d540); the code comment's ARM64-only explanation is wrong here.

bugs_issues.title: A refused Eraser probe is cached as 'absent': the store's deletes then run as plain SQL and leave the ledger statements of the deleted edges live

entry.title: A refused Eraser probe is cached as 'absent': the store's deletes then run as plain SQL and leave the ledger statements of the deleted edges live
entry.intended: iris_vector_graph/stores/iris_sql_store.py:1333-1338 (delete_nodes' docstring reserves the SQL path for 'an install with no ObjectScript classes, hence no ^KG to maintain'; here the classes, the ledger and ^KG all exist); INV-stmt / ERS-I2 (no live statement without its row, experiment/playbook-uplift/ontology/12-erasure.md:42). Context, not the anchor: docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md:511-514's ClassesUnreadable rule covers only a routines database the role cannot read (raised when the <PROTECT> names that database, iris_vector_graph/schema.py:119-143); for a refusal that names no database, a missing %Native_ClassExecution, the pin makes the opposite choice and lets 'absent' stand (schema.py:134-137; the engine's capability probe likewise, at DEBUG, schema.py:2828-2830). R206 (_dictionary.py:8-12) fixed the refused dictionary SELECT by asking natively and says nothing about a refused native call.
entry.observed: Live in AUDITB (ws-live-sql-fallback-priv), as the operator-authorised disposable principal, ledger enabled (not strict), 4 nodes and 2 recorded edges, verify() equal. With ADMIN_GUIDE's writing row (%DB_%DEFAULT:RW, %Native_ClassExecution:U, %Native_GlobalAccess:U, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE ON SCHEMA Graph_KG) engine.delete_node('sfp|a') and IRISGraphStore.delete_edges([('sfp|c','R','sfp|d')]) went through Graph.KG.Eraser (probe cache True) and the rows, the ^KG out entries and both ledger statements went. With the same role without %Native_ClassExecution the probe's native IDKEYExists raised '<PROTECT> *Resource %Native_ClassExecution required' (the run's DEBUG line 'Graph.KG.Eraser.EraseNodeIds taken as absent: ...'; that the dictionary SELECT was refused with -99 before it is read from _dictionary.py:48-56, not logged), and _has_eraser_method (iris_sql_store.py:1307-1318, except Exception -> False, cached for the store's life) took the Eraser as absent, logged at DEBUG only; both calls returned success through the SQL fallbacks (_delete_nodes_sql, iris_sql_store.py:1363-1418; delete_edges, :1504-1518), which deleted the rows and left both statements (^IVG.Ledger tuple and stmt, closed seq empty) live without their rows. No warning or error was raised. Any other exception of the probe (a transient driver or network error) takes the same path for the life of that store.
entry.remedy: Treat only a definite 'not compiled' answer as absent: re-raise (or raise ClassesUnreadable) on a refusal or any other probe error, do not cache a failed probe, and log the fallback at WARNING; or remove the SQL fallback for namespaces where the ledger or ^KG exists.
entry.notes: Filed by the orchestrator from the writer census (WS-OBL-147/148/150/154 were open as 'unreached at the pin's deploy'); id in the writesets lane's range (nn 50-69), that lane having finished. The role without %Native_ClassExecution departs from ADMIN_GUIDE's writing row; the defect is the silent fallback into a path the code reserves for installs without the classes, which breaks INV-stmt and reports success; any other probe exception (a transient driver or network error) takes the same path with no unusual role. Maintainer question: must a role without %Native_ClassExecution be refused, or served (the pin serves it elsewhere, schema.py:134-137), and if served, may the store's deletes fall back to SQL while the ledger and ^KG exist? Same pattern as the ledger guard's fail-open (F-0801) and the engine's native fallback (F-C1795). The five 'gref ... Returning a mock object' WARNING lines in each variant's log are emitted by the driver package's embedded-python shim (_iris_ep/_runtime_facade.py) on a lookup of iris.gref outside embedded Python; they appear identically with both roles and say nothing about the fallback.

bugs_issues.title: save_snapshot archives writes that never commit

entry.title: save_snapshot archives writes that never commit
entry.intended: decisions.md HD-1802 (working): claim a consistent snapshot only with quiescent writers or a verified snapshot/epoch protocol, and declare the quiet-writer premise for the current exporter; SNP-Q1.17.
entry.observed: Live (c18-live-dirty-export): another connection opened a transaction (TLEVEL 1) and created c18:ghost; save_snapshot ran; the writer rolled back; the DB holds 0 ghost rows, the archive holds {'kg_lines': [{'k': ['label', '0', 'C18Ghost', 'c18:ghost'], 'v': ''}], 'nodes': [{'created_at': '2026-11-13T23:05:06', 'graph_id': '', 'node_id': 'c18:ghost'}], 'rdf_props': [{'graph_id': '', 'key': 'p', 's': 'c18:ghost', 'val': 'uncommitted'}, {'graph_id': '', 'key': 'id', 's': 'c18:ghost', 'val': 'c18:ghost'}]}. Model: cmc-snap-as-built-committed (expected-violation, 36 states, exhaustive within bounds), cmc-snap-as-built-dangling (expected-violation, 63 states, exhaustive within bounds) (an edge archived without its endpoint), reviewed export gate cmc-snap-reviewed (pass, 65 states, exhaustive within bounds), control cmc-snap-ctl-gate (expected-violation, 36 states, exhaustive within bounds), witness cmc-snap-wit (expected-violation, 41 states, exhaustive within bounds). Neither USER_GUIDE.md:1151-1168 nor ADMIN_GUIDE.md:975-1010 declares a quiet-writer premise; the docstring says only 'reads only' (snapshot.py:803).
entry.remedy: Document the quiet-writer premise (HD-1802) and refuse or warn when transactions are open; or export under a namespace-wide export gate that writers respect.
entry.notes: Intent: HD-1802 is a working assumption; the observation (an archive can hold content that never existed, which a restore then makes real) is beyond 'not point in time' and holds under any reading.

bugs_issues.title: A revision whose changeset recorded nothing keeps the tenant's message, source, correlation id and idempotency key (and the key's binding) through a complete redaction

entry.title: A revision whose changeset recorded nothing keeps the tenant's message, source, correlation id and idempotency key (and the key's binding) through a complete redaction
entry.intended: specs/256-ledger-tenant-redaction/spec.md:42-44 (US1: after erase and redaction 'no record, revision field or index reachable through IVG holds the tenant's entity ids, attribute values or messages'); spec.md:121-123 (FR-004: 'For a revision whose every record is redacted, message, source, correlation_id and idempotency_key MUST be cleared'; a revision with no records has every record redacted); spec.md:142-143 (SC-001: a scan of every ^IVG.Ledger subscript and value and every Graph_KG.ledger_* row finds none of the tenant's ids or values, 'Zero matches is the bar'); specs/256-ledger-tenant-redaction/plan.md:25 (a redacted revision's key is moved from ^IVG.Ledger("idem") to idemRedacted so a retry neither replays nor re-creates).
entry.observed: Found by the randomized simulator (I6 SC-001 scan at each completed redaction) in 9 of 304 schedules, first seed 1033 (graph-per-tenant gamma) and in the prefix shape (seed 1087); shrunk through the product to 7 operations (sim-fcs01-ddmin-s1033) and hand-reduced to 6, reproduced 3/3 on AUDITA (sim-fcs01-minimal): commit(create_node acme|n1 with label Person, key acme-k-min-1) -> seq 2; commit(upsert_node acme|n1 + add_label acme|n1 Person, key acme-k-min-2, message 'acme commit min-2', source {tenant: acme}, correlation id acme-corr-0) -> seq 3 with op_count 0 (an existing node and an existing label are no-ops with no record, LedgerApply.cls:229-233, :252-263; the commit's empty check counts operations, not records, Ledger.cls:491-492, and writes the revision row and the idempotency binding regardless, Ledger.cls:523-525); delete_nodes_by_prefix('acme|'); ledger.redact(None, prefix='acme') -> complete, records_tombstoned 3, revision_seqs [2], redaction revision 4; verify() -> equal. Afterwards Graph_KG.ledger_revisions row 3 still holds message 'acme commit min-2', source {"n":2,"tenant":"acme"}, correlation_id 'acme-corr-0', idempotency_key 'acme-k-min-2'; ^IVG.Ledger("idem","acme-k-min-2") = $LB(3, fingerprint) is still bound while seq 2's key went to idemRedacted; a same-key retry after the redaction answers replayed=True with seq 3 instead of idempotency_redacted. Metadata is cleared only on a revision's first tombstone (LedgerRedact.cls:332-347, plan.md:25), and a revision with no records never receives one. The receipt and the redaction revision do not name revision 3.
entry.remedy: Give every committed revision something the target predicate can match, or do not create a revision that records nothing. Options: (a) a changeset whose operations all turn out to be no-ops returns the current head without writing a revision row or binding its key (spec 213 would have to say whether an all-no-op commit is a revision); (b) record each no-op operation as a content-free 'noop' record carrying the entity id and graph, so FR-001's predicate matches it and the first-tombstone rule clears the revision and unbinds the key; (c) at Final, clear the metadata of revisions with op_count 0 whose changeset named the target (needs the ids, which only (b) keeps). Extend the SC-001 test (spec.md:48-50) with a no-op changeset of the redacted tenant and a same-key retry after the redaction.
entry.notes: Severity S2 rather than S1: the residue is operator-supplied revision metadata and an idempotency binding, not recorded entity content; it is S1-class wherever operators put tenant identifiers in messages, sources, correlation ids or keys, as spec 256's own scenario and opsreview's per-tenant correlation ids do (client.py history() docstring). Not F-1301: that finding is FR-004's 'every' versus Decision 2's 'any' for spanning revisions; here both readings fail, because the plan's mechanism clears metadata only on a first tombstone. Not F-C1306 (non-default IVG Schema after an upgrade): this is the default schema on a fresh enable. Upsert of an existing node with identical properties, set_property with the current value and add_label of a present label all produce the same zero-record revision (FR-009c, LedgerApply.cls:252, :265).

entry.intended: ADJ-I5.9 / ADJ-I5.9.1; HD-0401 (assumption): invalidation never makes an old degree-cache value valid again.

entry.notes: adj_degree-as-built-F0401-erase gives the finding's trace; the refinement audit against L1 'degree = committed out count' fails as built and passes for the reviewed design. Live provocation is unrepresentable with the public surface: the window lies between the probe and the count inside one Adj.Degree call. Review-response reclassification (review R2-08 / R-11, condition 5; 2026-11-14): disposition changed from reproduced-model to intent-undecided. The intended behaviour rests only on HD-0401, an Assumption (decisions.md: 'invalidation can never make an old degree-cache value valid again' is the working choice; a per-source generation is named as an alternative) and on ADJ-I5.9, which restates it; no authoritative source settles it. The observed behaviour is unchanged and kept: as-built model breadth-a-mc-adj_degree-as-built and the located control proofs-breadth-hd0401-erase-kills-gen reproduce the trace (model-level; not provoked live). Conditional on HD-0401: a defect if the maintainer adopts it.

entry.intended: ALG-I2/ALG-I3 and the IVG schema boundary (spec 262: the IVG tables live in the IVG schema, Graph_KG here).
entry.observed: Live (b-10-live-scope): the deployed class method Graph.KG.PageRankEmbedded.ComputePageRank('b10_%', ...) answered {"raised": "RuntimeError: <THROW> *%Exception.PythonException <PYTHON EXCEPTION> 246 <class 'irisbuiltins.SQLError'>:  Table 'SQLUSER.NODES' not found"}: its unqualified table names resolve to SQLUser, outside the namespace's IVG schema, so the deployed class cannot run against the IVG tables at all here; where a SQLUser.nodes/rdf_edges exists it reads that table instead. The every-graph part is confirmed at the source only: ComputePageRankCore selects nodes and rdf_edges by node_id LIKE ? with no graph_id predicate (PageRankEmbedded.cls:5-30).
entry.remedy: Remove the class or scope it to one graph and the IVG schema (qualified table names).
entry.notes: No engine method calls it (inventory: direct-surface-only); reproduced branch: 'a table outside the IVG schema'.

bugs_issues.title: The stats row can lose counts

entry.title: The stats row can lose counts
entry.intended: docs/ledger-prometheus-hook.md:16 ('ledger_stats counts every process's commits, so it is the one to use for totals'); LED-B13.4 (each outcome adds exactly one); FR-051 (LedgerStats.cls:1-3).
entry.observed: Live AUDITB: (1) four processes x 1,000 Ledger.Count calls, each answering status 1, raised the counter by 3,865 (135 lost updates of the %OpenId/%Save read-modify-write; b-11-live-f1102-contention; 2 x 300 calls lost none in b-11-live-f1102-txn). (2) A commit nested in process A's caller transaction holds the stats row's lock until that transaction ends: process B's Count waited 10.0 s and failed with a %SaveData lock error that every caller ignores, so its count is lost (b-11-live-f1102-locktimeout); a refused commit or a guard refusal in another process therefore stalls 10 s too. (3) The finding's 'before-image wipes other processes' counts' did not occur: B is blocked by the row lock, not overwritten; instead B's save after A's rollback wrote its dirty copy and kept the rolled-back commit's count (new finding F-C1101). Model: m11-stats-as-built-rmw and m11-stats-as-built-caller-txn violate LED-B13.4; m11-stats-reviewed (atomic per-counter increments) passes; control m11-stats-control-split caught.
entry.remedy: Increment each counter atomically ($Increment on a mapped global, or UPDATE ... SET c = c + 1 outside the commit's transaction for refusals), count commits in a way a rollback takes back exactly, and never let a counter update wait on another process's transaction; or document the counters as approximate lower bounds.
entry.notes: Premise P-1103 is only partly true on IRIS 2026.1 Community: %OpenId takes no lock, but %Save's row lock inside a transaction is held to its end.

bugs_issues.title: Two first enables at once: the second fails instead of returning the genesis

entry.title: Two first enables at once: the second fails instead of returning the genesis
entry.intended: specs/213-graph-revision-ledger/contracts/ledger-api.md:22 (enable returns the genesis on the first call or the current head, idempotent); LED-B1.12; decisions.md HD-1104 (assumption: settings fixed at genesis; does not change idempotency).
entry.observed: Live AUDITB, two processes released together on a never-enabled ledger with 1,500 nodes: in 8 of 8 trials one Enable answered inconsistent and the other seq 1 (b-11-live-f1104). Two mechanisms: 6 trials 'revision row missing for seq 0': the second read the first's uncommitted state=enabled and head=0 on the unlocked fast path (Ledger.cls:254-260); 2 trials 'ID key not unique': the second had read never-enabled before the first set it, waited on the head lock and re-ran the genesis (:288-304, P-1106 confirmed). The ledger was left enabled at head 1 with one revision (rollback intact). Model: m11-enable-as-built violates LED-B1.12; m11-enable-as-built-consistency passes (LED-B1.7 holds); m11-enable-reviewed (lock first, then read state) passes; control m11-enable-control-nolock caught.
entry.remedy: Take the head lock before reading the state (or re-read it under the lock) in every branch, including the enabled fast path; a live test with two concurrent enable() calls.
entry.notes: The dirty-read branch is the more frequent cause on this build; the finding named only the genesis re-run.

bugs_issues.title: A register that fails after its upsert keeps the new settings

entry.notes: Model (main lane, explorer, exhaustive within bounds): as-built violates 'a refused register changes nothing' (upsert committed before LoadColumns throws); the links-change path reports 'rebuild pending' as documented (FHIRGraph.cls:262-271, pass); the reviewed design passes and its upsert-outside-transaction control is caught. Live reproduction is blocked-access: HS.FHIRServer.* classes and the HS_FHIRServer SQL schema (an IRIS for Health FHIR repository) are absent on IRIS Community 2026.1 in AUDITC: 0 classes, 0 tables, Register answers 'no FHIR repository' (live c15-live-register).
entry.title: A register that fails after its upsert keeps the new settings
entry.intended: SYS-I3 (a refused command leaves every store as it was); INT-F3.9.
entry.observed: Source: Register upserts Graph_KG.fhir_graphs (FHIRGraph.cls:235-245) with autocommit Exec and no TSTART, then runs Open, LoadColumns (LoadLinks, LoadCompartment, LoadProps, HS.FHIRServer.Schema.LoadSchema) and the json_links UPDATE (:247-258); the Catch (:276-278) returns an error without undoing the upsert. Live on Community (c15-live-register): every refusal reachable without a repository happens before the upsert and wrote 0 journal records, so the defect window cannot be entered here.
entry.model_hint: as-built: Register = [validate] -> upsert settings (autocommit) -> Open/LoadColumns may throw -> json_links UPDATE; a throw after the upsert returns error with new settings stored (violates 'refused => stores unchanged'). reviewed (decisions SYS-I3/INT-F3.9): validate and load columns first, then upsert + json_links in one transaction, so a refusal changes nothing. Negative control: reviewed with the upsert moved before validation must be caught.
entry.remedy: Validate and load metadata before writing, then do the upsert and the json_links update in one transaction (or roll back the upsert on failure).

entry.title: Four unit tests never run: each is shadowed by a later method of the same name in its test class (lint warning F811)
entry.intended: The product's lint gate is 'ruff check . - zero errors' (PRE_RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md:139-146; CONTRIBUTING.md:36-39 'Lint before you commit'), and its default rules include F811 (redefinition of an unused name). A test the suite contains is meant to run: CONTRIBUTING.md:175 ('Write the test before the code, and assert the answer'); pytest collects one function per name in a class, so a redefined test method replaces the earlier one.
entry.observed: ruff 0.15.14 (pg-lint-ruff) reports F811 at tests/unit/test_coverage_boost.py:307 and :319 (TestBulkLoader.test_load_networkx_empty_graph and test_load_networkx_with_nodes_and_edges redefine :234 and :245) and at tests/unit/test_engine_deep.py:399 (TestEmbedNodesMethod.test_embed_nodes_progress_callback redefines :367) and :1139 (TestEngineEmbedTextMethod.test_embed_text_embedder_returns_list redefines :1132). pytest --collect-only on the three classes collects each of these names once, and the class attribute is the later definition in all four cases (co_firstlineno 307, 319, 399, 1139; $RUN_DIR/product-gates/lint-r1/shadowed-collect.txt). Three of the four shadowed bodies check something their replacement does not: :234 patches BulkLoader._executemany_batched and _rebuild_indices (the replacement patches builtins.__import__ and passes build_globals=False); :245 builds nodes with a label= attribute (the replacement uses namespace= and asserts input counts); :367 sets an embedder on a fresh engine and asserts the result type (the replacement asserts only that a progress list exists). :1132 and :1139 are equivalent.
entry.remedy: Give each pair distinct names (or merge them) so both bodies run, after deciding which assertions are wanted; select F811 as an error in a [tool.ruff] table so the lint gate fails on a shadowed test.
entry.notes: Test-suite defect, not a product behaviour: the shadowed tests cover BulkLoader.load_networkx (modules 03/15) and engine.embed_nodes / embed_text (module 06). Found by the lane's 3.5-lint run. The other 60 of ruff's 64 F811 warnings were read by name: 58 in tests are pytest fixture parameters that rebind an imported fixture (pytest's usual pattern) or local re-imports, 1 is a notebook re-import, and 1 is in product code: iris_vector_graph/bolt_server.py:314 rebinds decode_messages to its stateless replacement on purpose, leaving the first definition (:269-291) dead; not a defect.

entry.title: A caller transaction with more than about 1,000 row writes to a table escalates to a table lock; every other process's write to that table, in any graph, then waits 10 s and fails with SQLCODE -110
entry.intended: No IVG document states whether one graph's (or tenant's) transaction may block writes to other graphs: a search of docs/, specs/ and README.md at the pin for lock escalation, LockThreshold or escalat* finds no statement on it; the multi-graph documents promise isolation of answers (SYS-I2), not of availability. The product neither documents nor configures the IRIS lock-escalation threshold (the engine default; iris-contract treats lock escalation as an engine feature). Intent undecided.
entry.observed: Live on AUDITD (structural lane, st-live-cap-batch, part '03 lock escalation'): with setAutoCommit(False), a caller transaction holding 200 create_node inserts leaves row locks only, and a second process's create_node succeeds in 0.03 s; holding 1,500 inserts, the lock table shows table locks ^t52S.XCFT.1 (nodes) and ^t52S.DMCe.1 (rdf_props) in mode X, and a second process's create_node of another node in another call waits 10.09 s and raises GraphWriteError SQLCODE -110 'nothing written' (its node is absent and the answer is consistent). Answers stay consistent; only availability across graphs is affected.
entry.remedy: Decide whether large caller transactions may block other graphs' writers; if not, document a batch limit below the escalation threshold or configure the threshold for IVG's tables, and say so in the operations guide.
entry.notes: Filed by the orchestrator from the structural lane's observation (the lane recorded it as intent-undecided without a finding). The st-live-cap-batch record is 'incomplete' overall because its Cypher UNWIND part was undecided (rerun as st-live-cap-batch-r2); the escalation part is decided in its log.

bugs_issues.title: A refused erase or adjacency rebuild (writer lock not granted) still leaves writes behind: the graph's no-lock mark, source generations and ^KG("__version")

entry.title: A refused erase or adjacency rebuild (writer lock not granted) still leaves writes behind: the graph's no-lock mark, source generations and ^KG("__version")
entry.intended: ADJ-X4.7 (ontology/04-adjacency.md, stated refusal): 'Removing a graph, removing all graphs and starting an adjacency rebuild are refused when the lock is not granted in 5 seconds. Nothing is written.' (implementing code iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Adjacency.cls:428-434, 452-458, 814-821; callers Eraser.cls:234-235, 788-789, TraversalBuild.cls:37-38). The erase contract: 'Erasure either completes or leaves the graph untouched' (iris_vector_graph/_engine/nodes_edges.py:1500-1507).
entry.observed: rx-live-04 (AUDITE, journal oracle, a second process holding ^IVG.AdjW exclusively, shown in ^$LOCK): erase_graph('rx04g') raised 'Adjacency.RemoveGraph: the writer lock for graph rx04g was not granted in 5 seconds' after 15.07 s, erase_all() raised the RemoveAll message after 20.07 s, sync() raised the BeginRebuild message after 5.00 s. Rows and ^KG out entries were restored (5 nodes, 3 edges, 10 out entries before and after), but the journal shows net changes that the rollback did not take back: ^IVG.AdjNoLock("rx04g") (and ^IVG.AdjNoLock(0) for erase_all), ^KG("gen","rx04g","rx04:a"|"rx04:b") (and ("gen",0,"rx04:d")), ^KG("__version"), and IRIS %iFind word entries ^t52S.DMCe.7("W",...) of rdf_props' idx_props_val_ifind; the refused BuildKG leaves ^KG("__version") bumped. Cause (source): the Eraser deletes the graph's rows before it calls RemoveGraph/RemoveAll (EraseGraph Eraser.cls:47-234, EraseAll Eraser.cls:709-788), the rows' adjacency hook (Graph.KG.AdjIndex -> Adjacency.Remove) calls WriterLock, which waits 5 s per row, then writes without the lock and raises the no-lock mark with $Increment (Adjacency.cls:51-73, documented as not undone by a rollback: ontology ADJ-T4.6.1), together with $Increment of ^KG("gen") and ^KG("__version"); BuildKG's Catch bumps ^KG("__version") (TraversalBuild.cls:155-163). Consequences: after a refused erase the graph keeps the no-lock mark, so readers store no degree for it until sync() or a later successful erase (ADJ-B4.6.5); the time to refusal is 5 s per deleted edge row plus 5 s (15 s for 2 edges, 20 s for 3), not 5 s. Content is not changed.
entry.remedy: Either take the graph's (or the parent's) writer lock in the Eraser and in BuildKG before any row is deleted or any counter is bumped, so the 5-second refusal comes first and writes nothing; or state the refusal as it is built: the content is untouched, but the no-lock mark, the source generations and the version stamp move, and the refusal comes after 5 seconds per row. Clearing the no-lock mark is a separate decision (it disables the graph's degree cache until a rebuild).
entry.notes: Exercised with an artificial long exclusive hold of ^IVG.AdjW by a second process; in the product only a reader's no-wait exclusive probe takes that lock exclusively, so the refusal is rare in practice. The %iFind word entries are IRIS's own index bookkeeping, listed for completeness, not attributed to IVG code. Not a duplicate: F-0409 (a failed rebuild in a caller transaction rolls back the caller's work) and F-C0402 (two rebuilds at once) are different defects.

bugs_issues.title: The embed queue serves PENDING entries in node-id order, so an entry can wait indefinitely

entry.title: The embed queue serves PENDING entries in node-id order, so an entry can wait indefinitely
entry.intended: A queue that is worked repeatedly eventually serves every entry (progress; HD-0604 single consumer).
entry.remedy: Serve in arrival order (a sequence subscript) or round-robin from the last reqId.
entry.notes: New, from the storage-order disposition (collation-ordered, not storage-ordered). A progress (AG EF) model with an unbounded arrival stream would show it; the bounded vec_queue model drains because arrivals are bounded.
entry.observed: ClaimPendingBatch and ProcessBatch take the first batchSize PENDING entries in reqId (= node id) collation order (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/EmbedQueue.cls:112-133, 258-268); under steady enqueueing of low-collating ids a high id is never reached.

bugs_issues.title: VectorOptimizer.migrate_to_optimized cannot run on IRIS 2026.1: its CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ... AS HNSW is rejected, so it copies nothing and answers success False

entry.title: VectorOptimizer.migrate_to_optimized cannot run on IRIS 2026.1: its CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ... AS HNSW is rejected, so it copies nothing and answers success False
entry.intended: README.md:12 and :21 ('Any IRIS 2025.1 or later works'); the method's own contract (iris_vector_graph/vector_utils.py:150-162: migrate the source table's vectors into kg_NodeEmbeddings_optimized and return migration results), and ADR-0006 as stated by VEC-X3.16 (the tool that fills the second legacy table checks the identity too).
entry.observed: Live in AUDITE (IRIS 2026.1 Community Build 234U, run rx-live-06, case 'VectorOptimizer.migrate_to_optimized copies rx06-src vectors into a table claimed for rx06-dst -> refused by the identity check'): with one vector in kg_NodeEmbeddings, migrate_to_optimized() returned {'success': False, 'reason': 'Migration error: <SQL ERROR>; Details: [SQLCODE: <-1>:<Invalid SQL statement>] ... < ON expected, NOT found ^ CREATE INDEX IF NOT>'} and copied nothing (kg_NodeEmbeddings_optimized 0 rows; journal: no net change). The statement at vector_utils.py:194-199 runs before the copy loop (vector_utils.py:205-249) and IRIS 2026.1 does not accept IF NOT EXISTS on CREATE INDEX, so the method fails on every call on this engine, whatever the data. As a consequence the missing identity check of F-0613 (no enforce_embedding_identity in the copy loop) cannot be observed live here: the tool fails earlier for an unrelated reason.
entry.remedy: Use a CREATE INDEX form every supported engine accepts (or probe for the index and skip the statement when it exists, as other setup code does), and run the identity check of F-0613 before the copy; add a live test of migrate_to_optimized on the oldest supported engine.
entry.notes: Found by the refusals lane while probing VEC-X3.16. Version-dependent: an engine that accepts CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS (not available here) would reach the copy loop and then show F-0613's unchecked copy. Related: F-0613 (confirmed-source).

bugs_issues.title: Dropping a neighborhood_vector index handle kills ^NKG("q") in the interned snapshot

entry.title: Dropping a neighborhood_vector index handle kills ^NKG("q") in the interned snapshot
entry.intended: ^NKG is owned by the adjacency module (04-adjacency.md:49, ADJ-0 'Stores owned ... ^NKG') with the algorithms module (10-algorithms.md:5-9); VEC owns its own index globals (06-vectors.md:8-9). Playbook §3.4: single write owner.
entry.observed: iris_vector_graph/_engine/vector.py:329-330 VectorMixin._neighborhood_index_drop runs Native API kill('^NKG', 'q') for any index name; index_protocol.py:50 routes the drop of a 'neighborhood_vector' index handle to it. The build and search of that index type are not implemented (vector.py:322-328 raise NotImplementedError). No other product site writes ^NKG("q") except Graph.KG.GraphIndex.DropNKG (Kill ^NKG) and the restore paths (st-check-own-census).

bugs_issues.title: Vector top-k searches cut equal scores in storage order

entry.title: Vector top-k searches cut equal scores in storage order
entry.intended: Playbook principle 5 (never depend on storage or insertion order, only on keys and explicit orderings; verification-playbook.txt:33-34); HD-0603's working assumption, a ranking contract with defined tie behaviour (decisions.md:83-85, intent/HD-0603.md:37-41); kg_KNN_VEC returns 'up to k (node_id, cosine) pairs, highest first' (docs/API_REFERENCE.md:955-971) with no tie rule. F-C0703 is the same defect for text search.
entry.observed: Live (st-live-perm-b, AUDITD): five nodes, three with the identical vector [1,0,0,0], stored in three insertion orders; kg_KNN_VEC('[1,0,0,0]', k=2) answered [pv:1, pv:2] (forward), [pv:3, pv:2] (reverse), [pv:2, pv:3] (shuffle): which tied node is cut depends on insertion order; with k=4 the same set comes back with the tied ranks reordered. Source: every vector top-k orders by score only (ORDER BY score DESC with no tie key: iris_vector_graph/_engine/vector.py:569-600 kg_KNN_VEC, :377-383 edge_vector_search, :819-829 the optimized path, :1264-1268 vector_search; the generated kg_KNN_VEC procedure iris_vector_graph/schema.py:2436-2482); module 17's adapter helpers have the same shape (iris_vector_graph/dbapi_utils.py:266-272, iris_vector_graph/stores/iris_sql_store.py:2633-2641).
entry.remedy: Order every vector top-k by a total key (score DESC, then node_id, or (s, p, o_id) for edges) in the SQL, the generated procedure and the adapter helpers, and state the tie rule in the API reference; a test that stores tied vectors in two orders and compares answers.
entry.notes: Severity follows F-C0703 (the text-search counterpart). The storage-order gate disposes these statements as 'ORDER BY present'; the reliance is the incomplete order at the cut, which only the row-permutation run shows. HD-0603 itself (kg_VECTOR_GRAPH_SEARCH's list(set(...))[:k], Python hash order) is intent-undecided and not part of this finding.

bugs_issues.title: Two embed-queue workers can work the same entry at once: the single-consumer premise is neither enforced nor documented

entry.title: Two embed-queue workers can work the same entry at once: the single-consumer premise is neither enforced nor documented
entry.intended: The embed queue is single-consumer by design (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/EmbedQueue.cls:22-25 'Single-processor', maintainer commit 5bb149ed; intent/HD-0604.md, status supported). Mechanism M-07 (semantics/mechanisms.json) law M07-L2: one worker per entry at a time, held by a claim or a lock, or refused.
entry.observed: Neither worker claims an entry: ClaimPendingBatch is a read-only scan of PENDING entries (EmbedQueue.cls:112-134) and ProcessBatch tests status PENDING and works the entry (EmbedQueue.cls:258-268); the Python worker process_embed_queue calls ClaimPendingBatch with no lock (iris_vector_graph/_engine/embeddings.py:1912-1915). Both the IRIS task (Graph.KG.EmbedQueueTask) and process_embed_queue are public, and no user document states the single-worker rule (docs/API_REFERENCE.md:1387-1416). Two IRIS processes calling ClaimPendingBatch were handed the same 3 entries (probe intent-a-hd0604-queue-claim). The generic queue machine shows two workers in flight on one entry (sem-mc-queue-as-built, check queue-embed-queue-as-built-HD0604, expected violation of M07-L2).
entry.remedy: Enforce one consumer per namespace (a lock held from claim to mark, or an atomic claim state per entry that a second worker skips), or document that only one of the two workers may run and refuse to start the second.
entry.notes: Semantics lane (steer 7): a hand-rolled variant of mechanism M-07 that departs from law M07-L2. HD-0604 records the design premise and leaves enforcement open; no earlier finding covered the departure (F-C0601 is the re-enqueue race with a single worker). Consequences: double model calls and the marks racing (with F-0604 and F-C0601).

bugs_issues.title: VectorOptimizer, a public class, hard-codes the Graph_KG schema, so in a namespace whose IVG Schema has another name it reads and writes the wrong tables

entry.title: VectorOptimizer, a public class, hard-codes the Graph_KG schema, so in a namespace whose IVG Schema has another name it reads and writes the wrong tables
entry.intended: docs/adr/0016-one-ivg-schema-per-namespace.md:10-12: every SQL object IVG creates lives in one schema, the IVG Schema, default Graph_KG, and a user may choose another name (IRISGraphEngine(schema_prefix=...) or IVG_SCHEMA_PREFIX); iris_vector_graph/__init__.py:94 and :123 export VectorOptimizer as public API.
entry.observed: Source at the pin: iris_vector_graph/vector_utils.py:22-26 sets _SCHEMA = "Graph_KG" (its comment: 'The embedding tables live in Graph_KG'); _qualify (:46-50) qualifies every table with it; the reads and writes at :295, :322 and :352 use it; VectorOptimizer.__init__ (:58-60) takes only a connection and never reads the namespace's recorded IVG Schema. The same comment (:22-25) says every method swallows a 'table not found' into a dict, so under another schema a call reports unavailability or does nothing rather than raising. Found by the style review round 2 (style-r2/STYLE-G2.md D-06-14, C-35; candidate N-06-a). Not run live.
entry.remedy: Resolve the namespace's recorded IVG Schema (as the engine does through schema_name) or take the engine or the schema name as a constructor argument, and stop turning 'table not found' into an empty answer.
entry.notes: Same pattern as F-1605 (the sample API's nodes field names Graph_KG) and F-1013 (PageRankEmbedded's unqualified SQL). Severity S4: the class is a maintenance utility (migrate_to_optimized, check_hnsw_availability, benchmark_vector_search); with the default schema it is unaffected.

bugs_issues.title: Text-search top-k answers and fused ranks depend on scan order

entry.title: Text-search top-k answers and fused ranks depend on scan order
entry.intended: Playbook principle 5 / gate 3.4-storage-order (never depend on storage or insertion order); decisions.md HD-0603/HD-0702 (a ranking contract with defined tie behaviour).
entry.observed: Source (storage-order check $RUN_DIR/checks/storage-order.json, dispositions in modules/07.json storage_order): engine kg_TXT's LIKE fallback takes `SELECT TOP k d.id, 1.0 AS score ... WHERE <LIKE terms> AND <graph>` with no ORDER BY (iris_vector_graph/_engine/vector.py:1041-1046), so which k matching documents answer, and their ranks, are the scan's; this is the path that ran on AUDITB (every kg_TXT score 1.0 in b-07-f0709, iFind index unusable). The iFind path (vector.py:979-985, :998-1003), the generated kg_TXT procedure (iris_vector_graph/schema.py:2484-2520) and kg_RRF_FUSE's ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) legs (schema.py:2557-2572) order by a score that ties (an occurrence count), so the TOP cut and the ranks among tied documents are the scan's; the ranks feed fusion (RRF adds 1/(c + rank)). TextSearchEngine's three helper queries order by (score, length) or (score, confidence) only (text_search.py:111-127, :165-178, :212-233). The engine's kg_RRF_FUSE sorts a Python set by score with no tie key (vector.py:1438-1452), so its tie order follows string-hash order, which differs per process.
entry.remedy: Order every top-k text query by a total key (score DESC, then the node id), give ROW_NUMBER() the same tie key, and break ties in the engine fusion by node id; a test that inserts tied documents in two orders and compares answers.
entry.notes: Not demonstrated live (two insertion orders) under the follow-up's no-IRIS instruction; the dependency is visible in the SQL text. The LIKE fallback is documented as unranked (scores 1.0, vector.py:925-930), but which documents survive the cut is not documented.

bugs_issues.title: The engine's index registry mis-decodes BM25Index.List: an index name holding a comma or a leading/trailing space is split or trimmed, so the real index is missing and phantom names appear

entry.title: The engine's index registry mis-decodes BM25Index.List: an index name holding a comma or a leading/trailing space is split or trimmed, so the real index is missing and phantom names appear
entry.intended: TXT-B9 (List names every BM25 index); TXT-B1.10 and the list_indexes/index docstrings (iris_vector_graph/_engine/vector.py:227-242, 260-266: the registry holds the indexes found when the engine starts; index(name) raises IndexNotFoundError for a name not in it). bm25_build and bm25_insert accept such names (BM25BuildInput only requires a non-empty name, iris_vector_graph/_validate.py:163-179; bm25_insert validates nothing).
entry.observed: Live (rx-dec-live-07, case 'index names holding the separator or a leading space'): bm25_insert('rxd,comma', ...) and bm25_insert(' rxdspace', ...) both created indexes; Graph.KG.BM25Index.List answered ' rxdspace,rxd,comma,rxdidx,rxdins'; _build_index_registry (Native API path: split(',') then strip(), iris_vector_graph/_engine/vector.py:106-118) gave bm25 names ['comma', 'rxd', 'rxdidx', 'rxdins', 'rxdspace']: the indexes 'rxd,comma' and ' rxdspace' are missing and 'rxd', 'comma', 'rxdspace' are phantoms (bm25_info on them answers no index). A fresh engine's registry, which list_indexes, index() and the RRF leg choice read, is the same.

entry.notes: The embedded-Python path (iris.gref walk) is not affected; this audit ran the Native API path the client takes over a remote connection.

bugs_issues.title: BM25Index.Build and Info write the graph name into their JSON escaping only backslash and quote: a graph name with a control character makes bm25_build raise JSONDecodeError after the index was rebui…

entry.title: BM25Index.Build and Info write the graph name into their JSON escaping only backslash and quote: a graph name with a control character makes bm25_build raise JSONDecodeError after the index was rebuilt, and the index's graph can no longer be read
entry.intended: TXT-B1.10 / TXT-D9 (the index records its graph and the engine reads it back through Info); RFC 8259 escaping as CHANGELOG.md:463-467 states for the search answers (the jsonEsc helper, iris_src/src/Graph/KG/TraversalBFS.cls:15-33); graph names with control characters are refused elsewhere (validate_graph_name, iris_vector_graph/_validate.py:19-49; ADR-0003), but bm25_build does not call it.
entry.observed: Live (rx-dec-live-07, case 'graph name with a tab'): bm25_build('rxdctl', ['name'], graph='rxd\tg') ran Build (^BM25Idx('rxdctl','cfg','graph') = 'rxd\tg' stored) and then raised JSONDecodeError 'Invalid control character'; Graph.KG.BM25Index.Info('rxdctl') answers '{"N":0,...,"graph":"rxd<TAB>g","schema":2}', which json.loads refuses; bm25_info raises JSONDecodeError and _index_graph swallows it and answers None (unknown). Build kills any index of that name before it writes (BM25Index.cls:99).
entry.remedy: Validate the graph with validate_graph_name in bm25_build before calling Build; escape with jsonEsc (or build the answer with %DynamicObject) in Build and Info.
entry.notes: Only an invalid graph name reaches it, so the impact is a confusing error after a destructive rebuild; recorded because the encoder/decoder pair disagrees on a value the server accepted.

bugs_issues.title: A rolled-back Cypher edge write leaves the interned snapshot's counters raised

entry.title: A rolled-back Cypher edge write leaves the interned snapshot's counters raised
entry.intended: SYS-I8 (CONTEXT.md:109-120): a store built from others matches them or says it is out of date; CYP-I6.4: a failed write query takes back all of its steps.
entry.observed: Live: with ^NKG built (engine.sync()), a query that creates edge b08_r1-[:B08NEW]->b08_r2 and then fails (duplicate literal edge) rolled back the row and the ^NKG(-1/-2) entries, but ^NKG(-3, idx(b08_r1)) went 1 -> 2 and ^NKG("$meta","edgeCount") 2 -> 3, with no stale mark (Adjacency.Put $Increments them, Adjacency.cls:95-107; $INCREMENT is not undone by TROLLBACK). The journal shows these records outside the transaction (b-08-live-footprints).
gates: 3.3a-writesets (^NKG counters written by every edge writer)
entry.remedy: Either keep the counters inside the transaction (SET from the merged degree, as BuildNKG's sweep does) or mark ^NKG stale when a writer's transaction rolls back; or document ^NKG(-3) and edgeCount as upper bounds (admin.py already treats edgeCount as an over-count).
entry.notes: Owning code is module 04 (Adjacency.cls) / module 10 (^NKG readers); found through module 08's rollback. No reader at the pin uses the ^NKG(-3) value except the rebuild (readers iterate it: NKGAccelAdjacency.cls:19, NKGAccelCentrality.cls:473); admin.py:808-816 knowingly tolerates edgeCount over-counts, so whether these counters are contract-bearing is undecided. The ^KG("gen") over-bump is documented as harmless (Adjacency.cls:23-30). Rerun under the iris lock after the 23:02:53-23:03:40 UTC incident window matched the original (b-08-live-fc0801-rollback-nkg-rerun, b-08-live-footprints-rerun).

bugs_issues.title: Schema procedures report one sampled element's property keys, chosen by storage order

entry.title: Schema procedures report one sampled element's property keys, chosen by storage order
entry.intended: db.schema.nodeTypeProperties / relTypeProperties list the property keys a label's nodes / a type's relationships hold (Neo4j procedure contract the handlers emulate: iris_vector_graph/engine.py:1333-1400); gate §3.4 storage-order: no answer depends on storage or insertion order.

WHERE p = ?` (engine.py:1382) with no ORDER BY, so the keys listed depend on which row storage order puts first.

bugs_issues.title: A Cypher DELETE deletes vector rows and reification rows itself, and only from the legacy vector table

entry.title: A Cypher DELETE deletes vector rows and reification rows itself, and only from the legacy vector table
entry.intended: The vector tables are VEC's (06-vectors.md:5-8: the routed kg_emb_<hash> tables and the three legacy tables), reifications are INT's (15-integrations.md:5-10: reify_edge, get_reifications, delete_reification). The Cypher module's Scope names writes of the graph tables (08-cypher-sql.md:5, CYP-D1 :40: nodes, rdf_labels, rdf_props, rdf_edges). Playbook §3.4: single write owner.

No statement names a routed kg_emb_/kg_eemb_ table.

Routed node tables carry a foreign key onto nodes (iris_vector_graph/_engine/schema.py:255-263, fk_{short}), so a DETACH DELETE of a node holding a routed vector may be refused whole or leave the vector, as F-0618 shows for the ledger's node delete; a live check would decide.

bugs_issues.title: Cypher range() with a step of 0 known only at run time answers [] instead of raising NumberOutOfRange

entry.title: Cypher range() with a step of 0 known only at run time answers [] instead of raising NumberOutOfRange
entry.intended: openCypher: range() with a step of 0 raises ArgumentError NumberOutOfRange at run time (vendor/opencypher/tck/features/expressions/list/List11.feature:115-130); the translator itself refuses a literal step of 0 with that error (iris_vector_graph/cypher/translator.py:29055-29099).
entry.observed: Live AUDITD (st-live-susp-range-step): RETURN range(1, 3, 0) raises ValueError 'range() step cannot be zero (NumberOutOfRange)'; UNWIND [0] AS s RETURN range(1, 3, s) and WITH 0 AS s RETURN range(1, 3, s) answer [] with no error (a run-time step of 1 answers [1, 2, 3]). entry.notes: Stated as built in CYP-T11.103. The TCK tests only literals, so the conformance harness does not see it.

bugs_issues.title: IVG.CypherEngine.Scalar answers the caller's default when the read fails, so a failed COUNT reads as 0

entry.title: IVG.CypherEngine.Scalar answers the caller's default when the read fails, so a failed COUNT reads as 0
entry.intended: IVG.CypherEngine's contract is {columns, rows, error}: 'a bad query is an error value, not a throw' (iris_src/src/IVG/CypherEngine.cls:12, :110; QueryJson :97-127 passes the error); execute_cypher answers a failed read with IVGResult.error and no rows (iris_vector_graph/_engine/query.py:1755-1757).

bugs_issues.title: Compiled native plan classes have no bound: one class per plan shape accumulates until a deploy

entry.title: Compiled native plan classes have no bound: one class per plan shape accumulates until a deploy
entry.intended: Playbook §3.6 capacity: a stated bound or measured limit for every resource that grows with use (gate 3.6-capacity, open text 'a bound or a measured limit for compiled classes'); NAT-T5.2: one compiled plan serves every read of its shape.
entry.observed: Inspected at the pin: Gen.Build compiles one class IVGC.P<hash> per plan-shape hash (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Cypher/Gen.cls:163-221) and records it in ^IVG.CypherCompiled; the only removal is DropAll (Gen.cls:225-230), called by setup's deploy (iris_vector_graph/schema.py:2939). No count, size or age bound and no eviction exist, so the namespace gains one compiled class (and its routines) per distinct shape (labels, keys, hop structure) for as long as the namespace lives, within the 32-bit hash space that F-0901 shows can collide.
entry.remedy: Bound the compiled-plan set (a count or LRU with DropAll of cold entries, or compile only shapes seen N times) and document the bound; or state that applications must not generate unbounded shapes.
entry.notes: Not measured live: running the native executor compiles product-generated classes into the namespace, which this lane left to the native-executor lane. Impact depends on how many distinct shapes an application issues.

bugs_issues.title: triangle_count, a read, creates twelve SQL functions (DDL, class compile, commit) and rewrites the deploy record, with no Arno library

entry.title: triangle_count, a read, creates twelve SQL functions (DDL, class compile, commit) and rewrites the deploy record, with no Arno library
entry.intended: ALG-I6: a read algorithm changes no content; it may write only its own work areas and caches (experiment/playbook-uplift/ontology/10-algorithms.md ALG-I6). The routine record ^IVG.Deploy("routines") is setup's record of what it created (iris_vector_graph/routine_record.py:1-21).
entry.observed: Live, journal oracle (b-10-live-fp): the first engine.triangle_count() in AUDITB (Arno library absent) wrote ['global:^IVG.Deploy', 'global:^oddDEP', 'global:^oddTSQL'] with no error, then answered from the LazyKG walk. The dictionary shows 16 classes Graph.KG.funcivgarnozf* created at that moment (b-10-live-fp-detail: TimeCreated $H 67888,3446-3447), i.e. the read path ran CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION for the $ZF wrappers and committed. A later triangle_count on a new connection rewrote ^IVG.Deploy("routines") again (1 journal record) although nothing was created. Source: execute_triangle_count tries the Arno path unless IVG_DISABLE_ARNO is set (iris_sql_store.py:3977-3988); build_kg_adjacency_chunked probes arno_available (arno_bridge.py:658-694), which runs _ensure_zf_call_function -> _create_routines: DDL + class compile + conn.commit(), refused inside a caller transaction (arno_bridge.py:106-136, :360-378), and RoutineRecord.save() writes the record on every probe (routine_record.py:93-95).
entry.remedy: Create the $ZF wrappers in setup (initialize_schema) only, and have the read path probe availability without DDL (or check IsAvailable first); save the routine record only when something was created.
entry.notes: Consequences: a read compiles classes in the reader's process (the compile-failure hazard F-0904 describes for module 09), commits, invalidates cached queries that call the wrappers, needs DDL privileges (a read-only login falls back silently), and inside a caller transaction is refused and falls back. The audit's own triangle_count call thereby compiled these twelve product SQL functions into AUDITB (product behavior, not an audit compile).

bugs_issues.title: The store's membership decoder refuses the Owner's components and label-propagation answers when a default-graph node is named 'components', 'communities' or 'largest' (read as an accelerated summary…

entry.title: The store's membership decoder refuses the Owner's components and label-propagation answers when a default-graph node is named 'components', 'communities' or 'largest' (read as an accelerated summary); the engine masks it by calling the Owner a second time
entry.intended: ALG-B3 (connected components group the default graph's nodes; Graph.KG.Algorithms.WCCJson answers a node->component map, iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Algorithms.cls:6-90); the decoder's own contract (iris_vector_graph/stores/iris_sql_store.py:662-676 docstring: Graph.KG.Algorithms answers with a map, which is a readable shape; only the accelerated summary is refused); the spec-230 reference in the product's code comments (e.g. iris_vector_graph/_engine/admin.py:306; there is no specs/230* at the pin) (an unreadable shape raises, a readable one is read). A node id is any string; nothing reserves these three.
entry.observed: Live (rx-dec-live-10, cases 'a default-graph node named largest'): default graph rxda->rxdb->rxdc->rxda, rxdc->largest, chain rxdx1..rxdx4, rxdd alone. Graph.KG.Algorithms.WCCJson answered the valid map {'largest':'largest','rxda':'largest',...,'rxdx4':'rxdx1'}; IRISGraphStore._execute_wcc answered rows [] with error "a summary, not a node→component_id map: it carries ['largest']" (AcceleratedSummaryShape from _membership_rows, iris_sql_store.py:670-675, _SUMMARY_KEYS iris_sql_store.py:636); CDLPJson likewise ('node→community_id'). kg_WCC and kg_CDLP still answered the wire map: on a store error they call the Owner again (iris_vector_graph/_engine/algorithms.py:816-828, 842-849).
entry.remedy: Tell the shapes apart by producer (the Owner path never answers a summary) or by structure (a summary's 'components' is a number and 'largest' a list; a component label is a node id string), not by the presence of a key that can be a node id.
entry.notes: User-visible answers stay right through the engine's second Owner call; the store result (and anything reading the store directly) reports a false error, and every such call runs the algorithm twice.

entry.intended: The graph-version token ^KG("__version") is in the adjacency module's owned stores (04-adjacency.md:49 ADJ-0; :64 ADJ-D15 'Each write that can change an answer moves it up'); ADR-0011 puts every rule that must hold on each adjacency write in Graph.KG.Adjacency (docs/adr/0011-the-adjacency-index-has-one-writer-module.md:12-30). entry.observed: iris_src/src/Graph/KG/ArnoAccel.cls:295-302 BumpVersion runs $Increment(^KG("__version")) and $Increment(^NKG("$meta","version")) outside Graph.KG.Adjacency (st-check-own-census: the only undeclared writer of ^KG("__version") besides the restore's _raise_kg_version, snapshot.py:57, covered by F-0404).

entry.title: The ^NKG centrality class methods called directly answer every graph merged; only the SQL functions refuse
entry.intended: An answer about a graph holds only that graph's data (SYS-I2); the product's own refusal says an algorithm over ^NKG with a named graph's edges present 'would be every graph's merged' (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/NKGAccel.cls:208-223, RefuseMergedGraphs; called by the kg_* SQL functions, iris_vector_graph/schema.py:2644-2665).
entry.observed: Live AUDITD (st-live-susp-nkg-merged): with nd:1->nd:2 in the default graph and ng:1->ng:2->ng:3->ng:4 in graph sgN and ^NKG built by engine.sync(), Graph.KG.NKGAccelCentrality.ClosenessGlobal over the Native API answers all six nodes of both graphs as one graph (ng:1 1.833, ng:2 1.5, nd:1 1, ...) and BetweennessGlobal answers ng:2 and ng:3 of graph sgN; SQL Graph_KG.kg_Closeness refuses the same state; engine.closeness_centrality() answers nd:1 and nd:2 only. bugs_issues.title: The ^NKG traversal class methods called directly (k-hop neighbours, shortest path, distinct k-hop count) answer every graph merged

entry.title: The ^NKG traversal class methods called directly (k-hop neighbours, shortest path, distinct k-hop count) answer every graph merged
entry.intended: An algorithm that takes no graph answers for the default graph alone and never mixes in a named graph's edges (ALG-I3, experiment/playbook-uplift/ontology/10-algorithms.md:45, citing docs/USER_GUIDE.md:767-775 and CONTEXT.md:97-101; SYS-I2). The product's own guard states why a reader of ^NKG cannot answer one graph: ^NKG holds every graph's edges with no graph key, and the ^NKG SQL functions refuse once a named graph has an edge so that plain SQL cannot get a mixed answer (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/NKGAccel.cls:213-223; ALG-B7, ALG-B7.2, 10-algorithms.md:129-131).
entry.observed: Live, AUDITD (st-live-reads3-10, oracle self-tested by st-control-reads3-selftest): default graph a-R->b, b-R->c, a-S->c, c-R->a; the same ids with edges a-R->c, c-R->a, a-R->d, d-R->b, b-S->a written in graphs stg1 and stg2, then engine.sync() (^NKG merges them). Over the Native API, with no graph argument: Graph.KG.NKGAccelTraversal.KHopNeighbors('a', 2, 1000) and its NKGAccel wrapper, KHopJson and KHopNeighborsSorted list node d (which exists only in the named graphs) at dist 1, totalNodes 3 -> 4; ShortestPathNKG('a', 'd', 10) answers {"hops":1} instead of {"hops":-1}; CountDistinctKHop('a', '', 2, 'out'|'both') estimate 3 -> 4. None of them changed when only edgeless nodes with labels/properties were added in the named graphs and properties on the default graph's nodes, so the change comes from the named graphs' edges. Their bodies read ^NKG(-1, ...) and ^NKG("$NI") with no graph key and no refusal (NKGAccelTraversal.cls:20-186, 366-553). In the same run BFSJson, which without the library answers from the default graph's ^KG (Traversal.BFSFastJsonSorted with graph ""), did not change.
entry.remedy: Give these readers the refusal the ^NKG SQL functions have (NKGAccel.RefuseMergedGraphs before reading ^NKG), or a graph argument that restricts the walk to one graph's edges; until then document that they answer every graph merged. Add a test with the same ids and edges in a named graph.
entry.notes: Companion of F-C1041 (centrality and community class methods, same mechanism) and F-1002 (RandomWalkJson). CountDistinctKHop is also reached by the product's Cypher approx_count_distinct route (query.py:4361-4404), which refuses USE GRAPH but checks no named graph; whether that public answer is wrong for an all-graphs read (CONTEXT.md All-graphs read: union of each graph's own answer) was not run here (module 08's surface), so the severity is kept at F-C1041's S3 for the direct class-method calls observed.

bugs_issues.title: The stats row can count a commit its caller rolled back

entry.title: The stats row can count a commit its caller rolled back
entry.intended: LED-B13.2 (kept revisions are counted in the commit's own transaction), LED-B13.4; docs/ledger-prometheus-hook.md:16 (ledger_stats is the one to use for totals); stats head_seq mirrors the ledger head.
entry.observed: Live AUDITB (b-11-live-f1102-txn): process A committed inside its own caller transaction (stats row saved: commits_ok 1->2, head_seq 1->2, row lock held to A's end); process B's Ledger.Count opened the row (dirty copy: commits_ok 2, head_seq 2), waited 2.5 s on the row lock; A rolled back (row restored to commits_ok 1, head_seq 1); B's %Save then wrote its whole dirty copy: final commits_ok 2 and head_seq 2 while the ledger head is 1 and only one commit is kept. Model m11-stats-as-built-caller-txn finds exactly this trace (read during the caller transaction, rollback, whole-row save).
entry.remedy: Same as F-1102: per-counter atomic increments (a refusal count must not write the commit count or head_seq), and derive head_seq from ^IVG.Ledger('head') at read time.
entry.notes: Distinct from F-1102 (lost counts): here the row over-counts and reports a head the ledger does not have. Root cause shared with F-1102 (whole-row %Save from an unlocked %OpenId copy).

bugs_issues.title: With SynchCommit=0 (the tested setting, IRIS default) an acknowledged ledger commit can be lost on an instance crash

entry.title: With SynchCommit=0 (the tested setting, IRIS default) an acknowledged ledger commit can be lost on an instance crash
entry.intended: A revision the ledger reports as committed exists afterwards (spec 213: a revision exists iff its mutations are visible; clients treat the returned revision as durable). No IVG document states a durability premise or the IRIS setting it needs.
entry.observed: Live: with iris.cpf SynchCommit=0 (the IRIS default: TCOMMIT returns before the journal is synced), a 36,000-operation commit acknowledged as seq 3 was entirely absent after a SIGKILL of the container and journal recovery; the ledger stayed consistent (head, revision rows, statement/tuple map, verify equal) and a retry with the same idempotency key committed once. The in-flight trial recovered all-or-nothing.
entry.remedy: Document the durability premise (SynchCommit=1 or a journal flush before acknowledging, or say that acknowledged revisions can be lost on a crash and that an idempotent retry recovers them), and consider checking the setting at enable().
entry.notes: Attributed to the tested IRIS configuration SynchCommit=0 (iris.cpf of the audit container).Environment premise rather than a code defect: the engine's documented default permits it. Exactly-once is preserved by the idempotency key; durability is not. The earlier run live-crash-world-r1-invalid exercised two crash/restart cycles without a commit in flight. Review-response reclassification (review R2-08 / R-11, condition 5; 2026-11-14): disposition changed from reproduced-live to intent-undecided, as the review asks. The record itself says no IVG document states a durability premise or the IRIS setting it needs, and calls it an environment premise; spec 213's 'a revision exists iff its mutations are visible' does not say across an instance crash.The premise is recorded in TRUST.md (durability needs SynchCommit=1 or a journal flush before acknowledging). Conditional on the maintainer's durability statement (STATUS residual question 7). Repeated (steer 10-11, incidents/SYNCHCOMMIT-WORLDS.md): under SynchCommit=0 an acknowledged commit was lost in 3 of 3 trials (live-crash-repeat-sc0); under SynchCommit=1 in 0 of 3 (live-crash-repeat-sc1; the container was restored to 0). The loss is attributable to the SynchCommit=0 setting; three trials are evidence, not proof that SynchCommit=1 suffices. Observed behaviour kept and still live: with SynchCommit=0 (env-synchcommit-setting) an acknowledged commit was absent after SIGKILL and journal recovery (live-crash-world-r2, one trial; repeated 3 of 3 in live-crash-repeat-sc0).

bugs_issues.title: Relationships the wire schema admits are refused once s+p+o exceed an undocumented key-length limit

entry.title: Relationships the wire schema admits are refused once s+p+o exceed an undocumented key-length limit
entry.intended: specs/213-graph-revision-ledger/contracts/changeset.schema.json:7-8 (NodeId maxLength 256, Name128 maxLength 128 for the tuple's s, o and p); Graph_KG.rdf_edges declares s, o_id VARCHAR(256) and p VARCHAR(128) (iris_vector_graph/schema.py:37-39).
entry.observed: Live AUDITC (corr-capacity): a commit of create_relationship with s = o of 194 characters and p of 97 commits; with s = o of 195 and p of 97 (and with 256/128) it is refused with failed_op 'insert relationship failed: ... <SUBSCRIPT>%SQLInsert+21^Graph.KG.rdfedges.1 ^t52S.BWr6.3(...)': the table's own unique index u_spo_graph_ekey (schema.py:44) cannot hold the key. The refusal is clean (nothing written). The ledger's tuple index ^IVG.Ledger("tuple", s, p, o, graphKey) would overflow one character later (s = o = 195, p = 97 still fits a read; read-only probe), so widening the table index would move the failure into AllocStmt (LedgerApply.cls:165) and genesis Capture (LedgerGenesis.cls:47). A ledger-bypassing create_edge is refused by the same index (SQLCODE -415).
entry.remedy: Document one combined key-length limit for (s, p, o, graph) that every store holding the tuple as subscripts can carry (rdf_edges' unique index, ^KG("out"/"in"), ^IVG.Ledger("tuple")), validate it before the transaction (client and ApplyAll) with its own error, and align the wire schema; or key the indexes by a hash of long values.
entry.notes: Clean failure, no corruption: availability and contract. Reproduce: experiment/playbook-completion/correspondence/tools/capacity.py.

bugs_issues.title: The commit does not enforce the wire schema's length limits, and reports violations as a ledger inconsistency

entry.title: The commit does not enforce the wire schema's length limits, and reports violations as a ledger inconsistency
entry.intended: changeset.schema.json: message maxLength 4000 (:189), idempotency_key maxLength 256 (:193), qualifier values maxLength 4000 (:46); errors.py:87-88 LedgerInconsistencyError 'The ledger's own structures disagree with each other'; CommitError codes (changeset.schema.json:288-311).
entry.observed: Live AUDITC (corr-capacity), every refusal clean (no state change): idempotency_key of 257 characters -> inconsistent 'revision row save failed: ERROR #7201 Datatype value ...' (LedgerRevision MAXLEN, Ledger.cls:554-555); of 600 -> inconsistent '<SUBSCRIPT> CommitInTxn+35^Graph.KG.Ledger.1 ^IVG.Ledger("idem",...)' (Ledger.cls:457); message of 4,001 -> inconsistent #7201; a qualifier value of 4,000,000 -> inconsistent '<MAXSTRING> %GetNext+30^%Iterator.Object.1'. Each surfaces in Python as LedgerInconsistencyError. Conversely a qualifier value of 1,000,000 characters (schema maximum 4000) is accepted and recorded.
entry.remedy: Validate the changeset and its metadata against the published limits before TSTART (and in Changeset.validate), refusing with a validation code (failed_op with op_index, or a new code) instead of 'inconsistent'; keep 'inconsistent' for disagreements of the ledger's own structures.
entry.notes: Operators alerting on LedgerInconsistencyError would page on an over-long idempotency key.

bugs_issues.title: A detach delete assigns statement ids to unrecorded incident edges in storage order

entry.title: A detach delete assigns statement ids to unrecorded incident edges in storage order
entry.intended: specs/213 FR-011 (detach cascades in statement-id order); playbook §3.4 storage-order / §3.6 row-permutation: results must not depend on row insertion order.
entry.observed: Live AUDITC (corr-row-permutation): a recorded node pm|1 with three unrecorded (ledger-bypassing) edges to pm|a, pm|b, pm|c inserted in the orders abc, cba, bca; delete_node(pm|1, detach) records the same three delete_rel records each time, but statement ids 1, 2, 3 go to the edges in insertion order (LedgerApply.cls:385-398: incident edges from a SELECT without ORDER BY; AllocStmt in cursor order). Recorded content without the ids is identical.
entry.remedy: Order the incident-edge SELECT by (s, p, o_id, graph_id) before allocating ids, if statement identity is meant to be a function of the logical state.
entry.notes: Working assumption: harmless (replay compares content; ids are internal), recorded because identical logical states give different histories. Review-response reclassification (review R2-08 / R-11, condition 5; 2026-11-14): disposition changed from reproduced-live to intent-undecided, to agree with the audit's own erratum for corr-row-permutation (evidence/errata.json: 'an order dependence whose intent is undecided; it is not a confirmed defect') and the correspondence matrix cell ('F-C1108 (intent-undecided)'); the record's notes take 'harmless' as a working assumption. Observed behaviour kept and still live (corr-row-permutation).

entry.title: Graph_KG.embedding_quarantine keeps a tenant's node ids and vectors through every erase and redaction, and the receipt does not say so
entry.intended: specs/256-ledger-tenant-redaction/spec.md:42-44 and 127-128 (FR-008 reach statement); docs/adr/0013-redaction-removes-content-from-history.md:47-48 ('Together they cover everything IVG can reach'). By design the quarantine is evidence, not content: iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Eraser.cls:300-302 and 756-758 (FR-039, FR-040); iris_vector_graph/_engine/schema.py:205-227 (node_id, vector, metadata, no graph).
