bugs_issues.title: The redaction's audit revision stores an unsalted SHA-256 of the tenant's name: a guessed tenant is confirmable from history

entry.title: The redaction's audit revision stores an unsalted SHA-256 of the tenant's name: a guessed tenant is confirmable from history
entry.intended: specs/256-ledger-tenant-redaction/spec.md:152-154 (Decision 1: the audit holds 'no entity id, attribute, value or free text from the target'); docs/adr/0013-redaction-removes-content-from-history.md:16 ('holds counts and sha256(graph NUL match) instead of the target's name. Nothing in it comes from the target'); spec.md:66-67 (US2: 'nobody can recover the content from the digest') against ADR-0013:43, 49 (record digests unsalted, 'can be confirmed by guessing').
entry.observed: Live digest (fu-r01a-snapshot-copies) and computation (fu-r10-target-digest): the redaction revision's source.target_sha256, readable through history() (which does not check the marker) and Graph_KG.ledger_revisions.source, is 5693ca28...c58d = SHA-256('' NUL 'fu1|') = Graph.KG.LedgerRedact.TargetDigest('', 'fu1|') (LedgerRedact.cls:56-59, :200, :433, :487). A 200,006-name dictionary confirmed exactly 'fu1' in 0.13 s (about 1.5 million guesses a second on one Python core). The marker and the receipt carry the same digest.
entry.remedy: Decide the intent (maintainer question): if the audit must not identify the tenant, store a keyed digest (HMAC with a namespace secret) or nothing; if confirmability is accepted, say so in ADR-0013 (as it already does for record digests) and drop 'Nothing in it comes from the target'. Reconcile spec 256 US2 with ADR-0013 Consequences.
entry.notes: Privacy: anyone who can read the ledger history can test whether a named tenant was redacted. Tenant names are low-entropy, so the digest is close to the name itself for this purpose. F-1301 records only the FR-004/Decision 2 conflict. intent-undecided between 'content-free' (spec Decision 1) and 'verifiable by an auditor' (ADR-0013:43).

bugs_issues.title: Schedule/Unschedule change the Task Manager task and the fhir_graphs task_id in separate, untransacted steps

entry.notes: Found by the footprint pass (footprints/15.json). Matters for durable tenant removal (HD-1502): an orphan task keeps re-filling an erased FHIR graph after a 'successful' unschedule.
entry.title: Schedule/Unschedule change the Task Manager task and the fhir_graphs task_id in separate, untransacted steps
entry.intended: SYS-I4 (a command that writes to more than one store writes all or none); INT-F9 (one sync task per graph); HD-1502 reviewed design needs an unschedule that verifiably stops refills.
entry.observed: Source: Schedule saves the %SYS.Task (FHIRGraph.cls:701, %Save) and only then records its id with a separate autocommit UPDATE Graph_KG.fhir_graphs SET task_id (:703); Unschedule deletes the task (:726) and then clears task_id (:729). No TSTART covers either pair. If the UPDATE fails after Schedule's %Save, a running sync task exists that fhir_graphs does not name: Unschedule then reports success without removing it, and the next Schedule creates a second task. Not run live: HS.FHIRServer.* classes and the HS_FHIRServer SQL schema (an IRIS for Health FHIR repository) are absent on IRIS Community 2026.1 in AUDITC: 0 classes, 0 tables, Register answers 'no FHIR repository' (live c15-live-register).
entry.remedy: Wrap the task change and the task_id update in one transaction (IRIS transactions span the IRISSYS and namespace databases), or make Unschedule find tasks by (TaskClass, NameSpace, GraphId) rather than by the stored id.

bugs_issues.title: delete_node removes the reifier nodes of the node's edges in a second transaction

entry.notes: delete_node is module 03's entry point (nodes_edges.py); recorded here because INT-E1.9 is a module-15 statement. The partial outcome is reported (SYS-I9 holds), but a crash between the two transactions leaves orphan reifiers silently (the F-1502 state). Orchestrator may re-home to module 03.
entry.title: delete_node removes the reifier nodes of the node's edges in a second transaction
entry.intended: SYS-I4 (all or none across stores); INT-E1.9 (deleting a node also deletes the reifier nodes of its edges).
entry.observed: Live (c15-live-reify, delete_node_parity): delete_node('c15:a2', graph='c15g1b') journaled two outermost transactions: the node, its edge and the rdf_reifications row in the first, the reifier node c15:reif2 (default graph) in the second. _delete_in_scope (nodes_edges.py:2176-2199) deletes reifiers after the node delete commits and, on failure, raises GraphWriteError 'the node is deleted; the reifier nodes of its edges (n) are not'.
entry.remedy: Delete the reifier nodes inside the same transaction as the node and its edges.

bugs_issues.title: The FHIR graph build writes the adjacency label index and the vector and document rows itself

entry.title: The FHIR graph build writes the adjacency label index and the vector and document rows itself
entry.intended: ^KG("label") is the adjacency module's (03-writes.md:43 WRT-D7 'owned by the adjacency module'; 04-adjacency.md:49), written by Graph.KG.Adjacency.PutLabel/RemoveLabel, which move the graph-version token; the label functional index calls them on each rdf_labels row (iris_vector_graph/schema.py:780, iris_src/src/Graph/KG/LabelIndex.cls:10-27). Vector and document rows are VEC's (06-vectors.md:5-8; 07-text-search.md:9-10). INT-F1.17 (15-integrations.md:94) says that with the functional index declared the row writes keep ^KG and the class skips its own Put/Remove.
entry.observed: iris_src/src/Graph/KG/FHIRGraph.cls sets ^KG("label",...) directly in SyncProps (:2566, unconditionally) and EnsureNode (:2616, unconditionally) and kills it in SyncProps (:2560) and DropNode (:2475-2477, :2491) when not indexed; DropNode deletes Graph_KG.docs, kg_NodeEmbeddings, kg_NodeEmbeddings_optimized and every routed node table (:2481-2489) and DeleteEdge deletes kg_EdgeEmbeddings and every routed edge table (:2588-2594) by its own SQL (st-check-own-census).
entry.remedy: Write labels only through the rows (indexed) or Graph.KG.Adjacency.PutLabel/RemoveLabel (not indexed), and delete a node's vectors and documents through the eraser's node path, so each store keeps one writer and the version token moves.
entry.notes: Consequence not demonstrated: in an indexed namespace the direct Set duplicates the hook's write; where the label index is not declared, label changes made here do not move ^KG("__version"), so a cached algorithm answer could outlive them (the F-0405 family). Confidence medium for that reason.

bugs_issues.title: Deleting a relationship with delete_edge or Cypher DELETE leaves its reification rows pointing at an edge that no longer exists

entry.title: Deleting a relationship with delete_edge or Cypher DELETE leaves its reification rows pointing at an edge that no longer exists
entry.intended: A reification belongs to its edge: rdf_reifications(reifier_id, edge_id) names the reified edge (iris_vector_graph/schema.py:514-519); delete_node removes the reifiers of a node's edges (INT-E1.9, F-C1502) and erase_graph deletes the rdf_reifications rows of the graph's edges (F-1502 observed), so a deleted edge has no reification.
entry.observed: Live AUDITD (st-live-fk): two edges reified (fr:r1, fr:r2); delete_edge('fr:1','R','fr:2') and MATCH (a {id:'fr:2'})-[r:R]->(b {id:'fr:3'}) DELETE r both answer success, and afterwards both rdf_reifications rows remain with edge_ids 6101 and 6102 that no rdf_edges row has; get_reifications(6101) still answers fr:r1 with its properties. rdf_reifications.edge_id has no foreign key (schema.py:514-519).
entry.remedy: Delete (or refuse to delete before removing) the edge's rdf_reifications rows and reifier nodes in delete_edge and in the Cypher relationship DELETE, in the same transaction, as delete_node intends; or declare a foreign key with ON DELETE CASCADE.
entry.notes: Edge ids are IDENTITY values and are not reused here, so a dangling row does not attach to a new edge; the reifier node and its properties survive (cf. F-1502 for erase_graph, F-1503 for delete_reification).

bugs_issues.title: A one-edge PROV lookup fails once the default graph's temporal history no longer fits one IRIS string

entry.title: A one-edge PROV lookup fails once the default graph's temporal history no longer fits one IRIS string
entry.intended: prov_as_dict maps one temporal edge (iris_vector_graph/_engine/prov.py:86-105) and prov_export_from_cypher the edges of the nodes a query returns (prov.py:141-175); INT-V1.6 (15-integrations.md:283) bounds only a window export ('Export a big history window by window'); module 05 has a paged reader for any window (iter_edges_in_window, spec 255).
entry.observed: Live AUDITD (st-live-cap-batch-r2): with 40,000 default-graph temporal edges whose JSON passes 3,641,144 characters, prov_as_dict of one edge and prov_export_from_cypher of one node both raise RuntimeError '<MAXSTRING>QueryWindow+27^Graph.KG.TemporalIndex.1', as does prov_export of the whole window; a one-second window exports. Both helpers read the whole default-graph window with QueryWindow(0, 9999999999) and filter in Python (prov.py:181-221). With short ids (st-live-cap-batch, window under the limit) all succeed.
entry.remedy: Read through the paged cursor (iter_edges_in_window with source or sources filters) or QueryWindow narrowed to the edge's timestamp and source, so a lookup's cost depends on its own edges, not on the whole history.
entry.notes: prov_as_dict's docstring says the whole window is read; it does not say the call fails past the string limit. The whole-window prov_export failure is the documented INT-V1.6 cap (its raising instead of logging is F-1501).

bugs_issues.title: Server and connection failures are reported as client syntax errors

entry.title: Server and connection failures are reported as client syntax errors
entry.intended: SYS-I9 (every refusal says why); Neo4j status codes distinguish ClientError (caller's fault, not retried) from TransientError/DatabaseError (P-1612); HTTP 4xx means the request was wrong.
entry.observed: Live (c16-s6-status-maps, stub engine, no IRIS): a lost IRIS connection answers HTTP 400 on /api/cypher and /db/{db}/query/v2, 400 + 'Neo.ClientError.Statement.SyntaxError' on /db/neo4j/tx/commit, and a Bolt FAILURE 'Neo.ClientError.Statement.SyntaxError' (classification ClientError, not retryable) both when the session's engine cannot connect and when a query's connection fails. Source: cypher_api.py:367-376, :396-400, :451-460; bolt_server.py:617-622 map every exception to those codes. Also: the sample API answers an unknown function as 400 UNDEFINED_VARIABLE (c16-s3, api/routers/cypher.py:231-247); the generated server's semantic_search swallows every error as [] (iris_vector_graph/gql/resolvers.py:85-88).
entry.remedy: Map connection/database failures to 5xx / Neo.TransientError.* (or DatabaseError) and keep SyntaxError for parse failures.
entry.notes: Disposition is confirmed-source: the probe ran the real server code (FastAPI app, Bolt TCP listener, neo4j driver) but the IRIS failure was simulated by a stub engine, not observed on IRIS. Interacts with retry policy: a correct transient code would let drivers retry, which is only safe once F-1601 is fixed.

bugs_issues.title: The generated GraphQL server pages nodes(label) over an unordered id list

entry.title: The generated GraphQL server pages nodes(label) over an unordered id list
entry.intended: A paged field (nodes(label, limit, offset), iris_vector_graph/gql/schema.py:150-156 -> gql/resolvers.py:32) is meant to page a defined sequence, so that consecutive pages partition the answer whatever the storage order (playbook principle 5, verification-playbook.txt:33-34). The sample API's own nodes field orders before it pages (api/gql/core/resolvers.py:159-177).
entry.observed: Live (st-live-so-confirm P16, AUDITD): five nodes of label Q written forward and in reverse; resolve_nodes(label='Q', limit=2, offset=0|2|4) answered pages [so16:0, so16:1] [so16:2, so16:3] [so16:4] forward and [so16:4, so16:3] [so16:2, so16:1] [so16:0] reverse; the permutation run (st-live-perm-c, module 16) shows three different first pages for three orders, while the sample API's ORDER BY created_at pages held. Source: SELECT s FROM rdf_labels WHERE label = ? with no ORDER BY, then all_ids[offset : offset + limit] (iris_vector_graph/gql/resolvers.py:32-46).
entry.remedy: ORDER BY s (and the graph) in the statement and page in SQL (TOP/offset over the ordered rows), scoped to one graph (F-1603).
entry.notes: F-1603 is the cross-graph part of the same resolver (the page is cut from every graph's ids); this finding is the order part and holds within one graph.

bugs_issues.title: The product's transaction premise 'measured on IRIS 2026.3 (driver 5.4.0)' is false on 2026.1 and 2026.2 with either driver: the driver is not its cause

entry.title: The product's transaction premise 'measured on IRIS 2026.3 (driver 5.4.0)' is false on 2026.1 and 2026.2 with either driver: the driver is not its cause
entry.intended: iris_vector_graph/_write_txn.py:15-17 and iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Txn.cls:7-8 state, as a measured fact, that SQL COMMIT and ROLLBACK end every level and START TRANSACTION inside a transaction does nothing; docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md:19-28 recommends 2026.1 or later and runs 2026.1 Community on every push.
entry.observed: Live, same 113 cases (cases.py --seed 20261114) on four engine x driver cells: SQL COMMIT and ROLLBACK at $TLEVEL 2 end ONE level (2 -> 1) and START TRANSACTION inside a level does nothing, on IRIS 2026.1 (Build 234U) and 2026.2 (Build 221U) Community, with intersystems-irispython 5.3.2 and 5.4.0 (ver-e261-d532, ver-e261-d540, ver-e262-d532, ver-e262-d540: the premise mutants sql-commit-ends-all / sql-rollback-ends-all killed by 2 and 4 cases in every cell), through both client entry points iris.dbapi.connect and iris.connect (ver-sql-entry-probe-e261, ver-sql-entry-probe-e262). The full contract (515 cases) holds unchanged on 2026.2 (ver-e262-d532-full). Driver 5.4.0 is therefore not the cause; the 2026.3 engine (the product cites irishealth:2026.3.0AI.113.0) cannot be obtained here (ver-avail-iris-2026.3), so whether 2026.3 behaves as stated stays unverified.
entry.remedy: State the premise per version (one level on 2026.1/2026.2; every level on 2026.3 if re-measured there), or drop it: the shape it justifies (Txn_Begin/End/Undo = TSTART/TCOMMIT/TROLLBACK 1) is right on every version measured. Re-measure on 2026.3 and record the build.
entry.notes: This is the version-difference record that iris-contract/CONTRACT.md ('Version difference recorded') calls 'F-C1701 candidate'; F-C1701 is already module 17's console-script finding, so the record takes the next free id. Impact on the as-built product is documentary: the main write path uses Txn_Begin/End/Undo, which behave as the product expects on both engines; the plain 4.6.3 path (namespace without Txn_Begin) refuses inside a caller transaction (_write_txn.py:26-28), and with no caller transaction START TRANSACTION + COMMIT/ROLLBACK at level 1 is correct under either reading. The engine attribution (2026.3) remains open. Separate driver observation (contract, not product): with 5.4.0, setAutoCommit(True) while autocommit is already on does not commit an open level (5.3.2 commits one), on both engines (ver-autocommit-probe-e261/-e262); the pin never calls setAutoCommit, so it has no product consequence (versions/VERSIONS.md).

bugs_issues.title: The pin's uv.lock installs intersystems-irispython 5.3.2, on which IVG answers scores as Decimal or text, raises on duplicate rows and refuses list parameters

entry.title: The pin's uv.lock installs intersystems-irispython 5.3.2, on which IVG answers scores as Decimal or text, raises on duplicate rows and refuses list parameters
entry.intended: pyproject.toml:42 asks only intersystems-iris>=1.0.0 and uv.lock:1358-1371 resolves it to intersystems-iris 5.3.3 / intersystems-irispython 5.3.2, so a uv sync of the pin installs this driver. Against it: OPS-B5.4 and iris_vector_graph/stores/iris_sql_store.py:1215-1220 (write_nodes / write_edges: 'A duplicate row is skipped'); the product's own tests and oracle: tests/e2e/test_460_proc_yield_alias_e2e.py:108 (a YIELDed score is int/float), the r306 algorithm oracle (scores equal the float reference), tests/e2e/test_460_r284_retrieve_rrf_score_e2e.py (retrieve() rrf_score is a float); the openCypher TCK scenario Unwind1 [3] (UNWIND of a list concatenation).
entry.observed: Driver A/B, alternating in time over the same files (validation/SUITES.md 'Driver A/B'). Under 5.3.2 (the uv.lock version): (a) Cypher CALL ivg.* YIELD scores come back as decimal.Decimal and retrieve()'s rrf_score as str ('.032522474881015332737'): 252 type-only failures in the r306 oracle (oracle-1), 289 in the gated subset, 2/2 rrf cases; (b) a duplicate INSERT inside write_txn surfaces as '<LIST ERROR> Incorrect list format, unsupported type for IRISList' instead of SQLCODE -119, so write_nodes / write_edges / create_edge raise GraphWriteError and write nothing (is_duplicate, iris_vector_graph/_write_txn.py:46-49, recognises only 'unique'/-119; intermittent per case, reproduced in every 5.3.2 run); (c) create_edge_temporal with temporal_structural_rows=True raises 'Cursor closed' (filed as F-C0502); (d) Cypher with list parameters or a list concatenation fails with '<PARAMETER ERROR> Invalid number of parameters' / '<ARGUMENT ERROR> Incorrect number of parameters' (TCK Unwind1 [3]; 14 gated e2e cases). Under 5.4.0 the same files pass: driver540-1 and driver540-2 237 passed (only F-C1002 fails) against driver532-1 224 passed / 14 failed; driver540-oracle-1 960/960 against oracle-1-c00 926/960; gated-540-1 138/138 against gated-532-1 119/138; gated-rag-540-1 2/2 against gated-rag-532-1 0/2; driver540-tck-unwind-1 14/14 against tck-1 and tck-unwind-rerun-1 13/14.
entry.remedy: Set a driver floor in pyproject.toml (the version CI tests, at least 5.4.0) and refresh uv.lock; type numeric result columns of Cypher procedure YIELDs and retrieve() explicitly; recognise the driver's duplicate-row error in is_duplicate.
entry.notes: Filed by the review-response lane (review R2-04) from validation/results.json rules decimal-score, duplicate-listerror, list-param-count and rrf-score-string (category 'product-defect (driver 5.3.2 from the pin's uv.lock)') and validation/SUITES.md 'Product-defect findings' item 1 (S2, high). CI tests a fresh resolution (.github/workflows/ci.yml), so it does not see the locked driver. For (a) the float type rests on the product's tests and oracle: docs/dev/driver-drift.md covers typed decoding of property values, not score columns, and shows 5.4.0 also decoding a SQL decimal as Decimal elsewhere. Driver versions after 5.4.0 not tested (offline).

bugs_issues.title: On a namespace that refuses the engine, close does not run: IRISGraphEngine has no close() and its store's close() is refused

entry.title: On a namespace that refuses the engine, close does not run: IRISGraphEngine has no close() and its store's close() is refused
entry.intended: OPS-X2.1.1 (ontology/17-operations.md): 'On a namespace that refuses the engine, most calls are refused. Setup, status, legacy removal and close still run.' Source of the exemption: EXEMPT_METHODS = {'initialize_schema', 'status', 'remove_legacy_objects', 'close'} (iris_vector_graph/schema_name.py:376-377, 'What a namespace that refuses an engine still lets it do').
entry.observed: Live (rx-live-17, AUDITE recording Graph_KG): IRISGraphEngine(conn, schema_prefix='RX17ALT') is refused at first access; create_node, get_node, node_count, execute_cypher and the store's get_nodes raise IVGSchemaError, status() and remove_legacy_objects(dry_run=True) run, but hasattr(engine, 'close') is False (the exemption names a method the engine does not define), and engine._store.close() raises IVGSchemaError: the store's methods are guarded with no exemptions (engine.py:388-390 guard_methods(self._store)), so its close (a no-op, iris_sql_store.py:4278-4279) is refused. The refusal itself holds; only the close clause does not.
entry.remedy: Either give the engine a close() (releasing what it holds) and exempt the store's close from the guard, or drop 'close' from EXEMPT_METHODS and from the stated behaviour.
entry.notes: Found by the refusals lane's mechanical audit of OPS X statements. Consequence is small (the store close is a no-op); the defect is the stated exemption.

bugs_issues.title: kill_query cannot end any process on IRIS 2026.1: %SYSTEM.SYS.KillProcess is not an SQL function (SQLCODE -359), so every call answers False

entry.title: kill_query cannot end any process on IRIS 2026.1: %SYSTEM.SYS.KillProcess is not an SQL function (SQLCODE -359), so every call answers False
entry.intended: docs/API_REFERENCE.md:2686-2692 'kill_query(query_id) ... End the IRIS process with ID query_id (an id from list_active_queries)'; iris_vector_graph/_engine/admin.py:957-962 'Calls %SYSTEM.SYS.KillProcess through SQL. True when the statement ran ...; False when it failed'.
entry.observed: Live (rx-live-17, AUDITE, IRIS 2026.1 Community Build 234U, driver 5.3.2): engine.kill_query on the lane's own scratch process (pid 140416, an ordinary killable client process) answered False and logged 'kill_query 140416 failed: [SQLCODE: <-359>:<SQL Function (function stored procedure) not found>] ... User defined SQL function %SYSTEM.SYS.KILLPROCESS does not exist'; the process answered %SYSTEM.SYS.ProcessID afterwards (still alive). The same -359 for pid 999999999. The statement 'SELECT %SYSTEM.SYS.KillProcess(?)' (admin.py:964-965) cannot run, so the documented operation never ends a process; the refusal branch (OPS-X3.5.1: warning, False) is the only reachable one. The upstream unit tests mock the cursor (test_admin_unit.py TestKillQuery), so they cannot see it.
entry.remedy: Call the class method through the Native API (classMethodValue('%SYSTEM.SYS', 'KillProcess', pid)) or through a projected stored procedure, check its return status, and answer False (or raise) when the process was not ended; add a live test that ends a scratch process.
entry.notes: Not tested on Enterprise or 2026.2/2026.3; the %SYSTEM.SYS class is the same in each, but whether any build projects KillProcess as an SQL function was not checked.

bugs_issues.title: The enterprise web gateway recipe lets any address manage the gateway and connects to IRIS as _SYSTEM with the stock password

entry.title: The enterprise web gateway recipe lets any address manage the gateway and connects to IRIS as _SYSTEM with the stock password
entry.intended: A deploy recipe does not expose an administration surface to every address with known credentials (deploy/README.md and docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md treat credentials and network exposure as operator settings; F-1710 for the other docker recipe).
entry.observed: Inspected at the pin (not deployed): docker/enterprise/webgateway-init.sh:12-31 writes CSP.ini with System_Manager=*.*.*.* (the gateway's management pages from any client address) and [LOCAL] Username=_SYSTEM, Password=]]]U1lT (the gateway's obfuscated form of 'SYS'); docker/enterprise/docker-compose-2026.yml:28-29 publishes the gateway on host port 64780 and :5-6 IRIS's superserver on 4972, both on every host interface; merge.cpf:4 keeps _SYSTEM's password from ever expiring or being forced to change. Only .iris-dev.toml refers to the recipe.
entry.remedy: Restrict System_Manager to the loopback/container network, bind published ports to 127.0.0.1, take the IRIS credentials from a secret and require a password change, and label the recipe as a local developer setup.
entry.notes: A licensed developer recipe; inspection only, as asked (not deployed). The compose file's ./docker/enterprise/ mount paths resolve against its own directory (ontology-2's separate note), so it may not start as written.

bugs_issues.title: IRISGraphStore.query_nodes(limit=n) cuts an unordered node scan

entry.title: IRISGraphStore.query_nodes(limit=n) cuts an unordered node scan
entry.intended: A capped read answers a defined subset (playbook principle 5; store_protocol.py:10-11 states no order); the same lane's F-C0302 is the engine counterpart.
entry.observed: Source at the pin: without a label, query_nodes runs SELECT node_id FROM <schema>.nodes FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY with no ORDER BY (iris_vector_graph/stores/iris_sql_store.py:1176-1181), so the n nodes answered (and then filtered by property) are the first n in scan order. The product call itself cannot be observed answering here: it kills the client process first (F-C1743, st-live-so-confirm P17). The same unordered prefix in the TOP spelling, sent by a harness cursor over the same data, answered [so17:0, so17:1] forward and [so17:4, so17:3] reverse (st-live-so-17b).
entry.remedy: ORDER BY node_id (and graph) before the cut, with TOP n rather than FETCH FIRST (see F-C1743), and scope the read to one graph (F-1701).
entry.notes: The property filter that follows reads by (s, key) in any graph (F-1701). Disposition stays confirmed-source: the live answer shown is a harness statement of the same shape, not the product call.

bugs_issues.title: When its dedicated Native API connection is refused (licence units exhausted), the engine silently uses the caller's connection and retries the refused connect on every native call

entry.title: When its dedicated Native API connection is refused (licence units exhausted), the engine silently uses the caller's connection and retries the refused connect on every native call
entry.intended: iris_vector_graph/engine.py:1895-1898: the dedicated connection exists because mixing iris.createIRIS() and cursor DDL on the same connection 'permanently corrupts the IRIS Python driver's parameter binding state'; :1913-1918: the caller's connection is used only 'when [the credentials] are not known'. The product's convention against swallowed failures (C-17, product-gates/STYLE.md) asks that a failed step be reported.
entry.observed: Live (live-licence-world, AUDITE, IRIS Community 2026.1, 8 licence units): an engine from IRISGraphEngine.from_connect, then 7 idle connections taking every free unit (the 8th refused 'Unable to allocate a license'); the engine's first native call (ledger enable/commit) could not open its dedicated connection; engine._native_conn stayed None and the calls ran on the caller's own connection (engine.py:1940-1941, except Exception: return _create(self.conn)), with no warning or error logged. Each later native call tried the refused connect again: two 150- and 3-operation commits took 2,062.6 ms and 2,017.0 ms against 47.3 ms and 1.46 ms with units free (control world C, registered run r2; an earlier failed harness attempt r1 showed 209 ms and 1.6 ms for the control). The commits stayed all-or-nothing, parameterised reads stayed correct and verify() was equal in this sequence; the driver-state corruption the comment names was not observed. With units exhausted before connecting, from_connect raised the licence error and nothing was written.
entry.remedy: Log the refused dedicated connect and either raise or record the degraded mode once (do not retry the connect on every native call); if sharing the caller's connection is unsafe, as the comment says, refuse instead of falling back.
entry.notes: Failure scenario S6 (licence refusal at product level), run by the orchestrator while no lane used the container; the style lane had read the same lines as a borderline C-17 case from source. Its id (nn 95) lies in the product-gates lane's range; the orchestrator filed it, after that lane had finished.

bugs_issues.title: save_snapshot and restore_snapshot hold the whole archive in client memory: about 11 MB per 1,000 edges, 190 times the archive's size

entry.title: save_snapshot and restore_snapshot hold the whole archive in client memory: about 11 MB per 1,000 edges, 190 times the archive's size
entry.intended: Playbook §3.6 capacity: a stated bound or measured limit for every resource that grows with the data. save_snapshot documents 'the whole database's graph content' (iris_vector_graph/_engine/snapshot.py:803-815) and states no memory bound; no IVG document gives one.
entry.observed: Live AUDITD (st-live-cap-snapshot-mem): peak client allocation of save_snapshot 21.3 / 89.2 / 356.1 MB and of restore_snapshot 21.8 / 84.6 / 338.4 MB for 2,000 / 8,000 / 32,000 edges (archives of 0.12 / 0.48 / 1.9 MB); save takes 7 / 28 / 108 s. save_snapshot fetches every row of every table with fetchall() and builds every NDJSON member as a list in memory before writing (snapshot.py:864-900); restore reads every member into memory (snapshot.py:1107-1112). By extrapolation a namespace of a million edges needs about 11 GB on the client; nothing refuses or streams.
entry.remedy: Stream each table into its ZIP member with a server-side cursor in pages (zipfile open(..., 'w') per member) and restore member by member in batches; until then document the memory needed per edge and a size above which snapshots are refused.
entry.notes: The million-edge figure is a linear extrapolation of three points, not measured. Cf. F-1510 (RDF export claims bounded memory); here no claim is made, so the defect is the missing capacity contract plus the amplification.

entry.title: In sync mode a failed build runs in the reader's own process
entry.intended: specs/257-compiled-native-plans/spec.md:60-63 (User Story 3: compilation never costs a caller); NAT-B5.3 (a failed build never stops the reader's own process from running SQL).
entry.observed: Live (b-09-f0904-sync-failed-build, Community 2026.1): with the product's test hook ^IVG.CypherGen("breaktest") a sync-mode read compiled a broken class in the reader's process (entry status ['ERROR #5475: Error compiling routine: IVGC.P1634875687.1.  Errors:  ERROR: IVGC.']); the read answered [['kb']] (31.8 ms). The same process then prepared 3 statement texts it had never run: ['ok', 'ok', 'ok']; the SQL path in that process answered [['kb']]. Premise P-0903 (observed by the product on 2026.3) did not reproduce here.
entry.remedy: Build in a job in every mode and let sync wait for the job, or document sync as a test-only mode with this hazard.
entry.notes: The mechanism (sync compiles in the reader's process, costing it the compile time) is source-confirmed; the harsher effect (the process can no longer prepare SQL) is an IRIS 2026.3 premise that Community 2026.1 did not show. Whether sync is a supported production mode is not settled: ADMIN_GUIDE offers it (docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md:746-752), spec 257 US3 promises compilation never costs a caller.

bugs_issues.title: The sample API lets two threads use its one IRIS connection at once

entry.title: The sample API lets two threads use its one IRIS connection at once
entry.intended: API-B4.5: two calls never use the one IRIS connection at once (DB-API threadsafety 1, P-1605; CHANGELOG 4.6.5 fixed the same pattern in cypher_api with _engine_lock).
entry.observed: Source: no lock around the shared connection (api/main.py:100-113 health is a sync def run on the thread pool; api/routers/cypher.py:94 is async with blocking DB calls on the event loop). Live (c16-s3-graphql-sample-api): 12 s with two threads on /health and one on /api/cypher: 6,943 health probes and 3,184 queries, 0 non-200 answers and 0 wrong counts on IRIS Community 2026.1 with intersystems-irispython 5.3.2.
entry.remedy: Serialize use of the connection (as cypher_api._engine) or use one connection per request.
entry.notes: The overlap was exercised but the failure (SQLCODE -400 seen upstream on 2026.3 AI with driver 5.4.1) did not occur on this build/driver. The code still relies on an unproved premise; obligation stays open.

bugs_issues.title: The REST dispatcher may read only the first chunk of a large request body

entry.title: The REST dispatcher may read only the first chunk of a large request body
entry.intended: API-B11.12: the routes read a request body of any size.
entry.observed: The finding rests on premise P-1607 (Read() with no length returns at most 32,000 characters). On IRIS Community 2026.1 the premise does not hold for the CSP request stream classes: a 50,000-character stream read with Read() and no length returned all 50,000 characters for %CSP.BinaryStream, %CSP.CharacterStream and %Stream.TmpCharacter (Native API invoke, c16-s5-fraud-sql-stream; ObjectScript in a terminal, c16-s8-followup: %CSP.BinaryStream=50000;%CSP.CharacterStream=50000;%Stream.TmpCharacter=50000;). End-to-end through a web application is blocked: no web application in the instance dispatches to Graph.KG.Service (Security.Applications read, $RUN_DIR/breadth-c/16/webapps.txt) and creating one changes instance security, which lanes may not do.
entry.remedy: None needed for the 32,000 premise on this build; keep a large-body test (bodies past the long-string limit still fail at %FromJSON of one string).
entry.notes: blocked-access for the end-to-end check: dependency = a %CSP.REST web application dispatching to Graph.KG.Service (Graph.KG.Service.CreateWebApp), which modifies Security.Applications. Other IRIS versions may still default to 32,000 (documented %Stream.Object.Read signature).

bugs_issues.title: Candidate: with the adjacency index declared, a failed rebuild could leave part of the adjacency missing

entry.title: Candidate: with the adjacency index declared, a failed rebuild could leave part of the adjacency missing
entry.intended: TraversalBuild.BuildKG's comment (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/TraversalBuild.cls:46-55): the kill sits inside the transaction so a row the rebuild cannot process leaves the adjacency as it was, never destroyed.
entry.remedy: Build the new adjacency beside the old one and publish it atomically, or keep the indexed path's purge inside a transaction it can roll back (no parallel jobs), or validate every row's graph key before purging.
entry.notes: Candidate from the journal (J12: ^KG out/in refilled outside any transaction by the caller's and two worker processes) against the method's comment: the indexed path purges and refills after TCommit with %BuildIndices in parallel jobs. Not reproduced: a sync() failed on a row with graph_id '0' left all 400 sources of a 400-edge graph in ^KG out and verify_graph ok. Readers during the refill can still see a partial adjacency (the method's own catch comment says so); that window was not measured. Not counted as a defect.

observed.verdict: adjacency intact after the failed rebuild

bugs_issues.title: EraseAll kills ^ArnoKG, a store the erase plan (GraphStores.Inventory) does not list

entry.title: EraseAll kills ^ArnoKG, a store the erase plan (GraphStores.Inventory) does not list
entry.intended: Graph.KG.GraphStores.Inventory is the product's list of the stores erasure covers (12-erasure.md:5 Scope; iris_src/src/Graph/KG/GraphStores.cls:28-130, 'Stated once here rather than rediscovered by each consumer'). ^ArnoKG belongs to the algorithms module's Arno bridge (10-algorithms.md:5-8). Playbook §3.4: single write owner.
entry.observed: iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Eraser.cls:806 (EraseAll) runs Kill ^ArnoKG; GraphStores.Inventory has no ^ArnoKG entry; EraseGraph and EraseNodes write no ^ArnoKG (st-check-own-census).
entry.remedy: List ^ArnoKG in GraphStores.Inventory (with the scope it can be erased by) and clear it through the Arno bridge's own invalidation (NKGAccelLoader.InvalidateAdjCache).
entry.notes: The kill itself is the right effect for an erase-all (ADR-0004). Not checked here: whether a graph erasure (which does not touch ^ArnoKG) leaves an Arno-path answer built from the erased graph's cached adjacency; that is an erasure-completeness question for the owning lanes. Refuted (orchestrator, from the ontology-2 lane's correction, checked at the pin): GraphStores.Inventory does list ^ArnoKG at GraphStores.cls:131, one line past the range the record cited (28-130); that entry itself says erasing content without bumping ^KG("__version") leaves Arno serving the erased graph, which is an erasure-completeness question, not this finding.

bugs_issues.title: IRISGraphStore.query_nodes(limit=n) without a label filter kills the calling Python process (SIGSEGV) on the pin's locked driver 5.3.2: it sends FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY, which the product's own FETCH…

entry.title: IRISGraphStore.query_nodes(limit=n) without a label filter kills the calling Python process (SIGSEGV) on the pin's locked driver 5.3.2: it sends FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY, which the product's own FETCH FIRST guard is never asked about
entry.intended: iris_vector_graph/stores/iris_sql_store.py:1162-1181 (IRISGraphStore.query_nodes, public method of the store adapter) answers an IVGResult; its comment (lines 1177-1178) states the driver segfault on FETCH FIRST is the ARM64 driver's with a parameter placeholder and is avoided by inlining the limit as a literal. The product knows FETCH FIRST can crash the client: iris_vector_graph/engine.py:726-840 (_fetch_first_unsafe) runs a FETCH FIRST probe in a subprocess 'because the crash is a hard SIGSEGV - uncatchable in-process' and falls back to TOP; engine.py:794-795 records Community 2026.1 as taking FETCH FIRST (refusing only an ORDER BY of an aggregate). The pin's uv.lock installs intersystems-irispython 5.3.2 (F-C1706).
entry.observed: IRIS 2026.1 Community (Build 234U), x86_64, driver 5.3.2: every FETCH FIRST form (FETCH FIRST 0 / 2 ROWS ONLY with and without ORDER BY, OFFSET ... FETCH NEXT) ends the client Python process with SIGSEGV (returncode -11) in a child process while TOP and LIMIT answer and the server logs nothing (env2-fetchfirst-probe). Through the pin (AUDITCORE, the pin's deployed classes and schema, each call in a child process): IRISGraphStore(conn, namespace).query_nodes(limit=2) with no label filter ended the process with SIGSEGV; the control query_nodes(label_filter=..., limit=2) (no FETCH FIRST) answered; execute_cypher with LIMIT answered (env2-fc1720-query-nodes). With driver 5.4.0 every FETCH FIRST form answers and query_nodes(limit=2) returns (env2-fetchfirst-probe-d540, env2-fc1720-query-nodes-d540): the crash is the locked driver's, the SQL is accepted by the engine.
entry.remedy: Do not emit FETCH FIRST from query_nodes: use TOP n (as the engine's own readers do, nodes_edges.py:810, 882), or consult the engine's _fetch_first_unsafe guard; with the driver floor F-C1706 asks for (5.4.0 or later) the statement is also safe. Correct the comment at iris_sql_store.py:1177-1178 and the 2026.1 note at engine.py:794-795, which do not describe this driver.
entry.notes: Reachability: query_nodes is a public method of the SQL store adapter; the engine reaches it only for stores without the native_sql capability (_engine/query.py:2286-2340), so the IRIS engine's own Cypher path does not (both execute_cypher probes answered). The process dies, not just the call: an API server or MCP process using the adapter this way stops serving every request. Distinct from F-C1706 (same driver, different symptom: a crash rather than wrong types or errors). Found by the contract-2 lane's TOP / LIMIT / FETCH FIRST coverage (X2-TOP); FETCH FIRST stays outside the contract (P2-FETCH). The product's engine.py probe classifies this build as unsafe for a different reason than the one it logs (it would log the SIGSEGV branch, naming AI builds and a JOIN). Duplicate of F-C1743 (structural lane, filed first); its evidence is merged there. Not counted separately.
